Its exterior product with $\beta _ z$ is $p^*(\mu \wedge \beta )=0$, since $\mu \wedge \beta $ has bidegree $(n+1,n+1)$ on $\mathbb C^ n$, and its exterior product with $\beta _ w$ is $g(z)\, \mathrm dV_{2n}(z)\wedge \mathrm dV_2(w)$, the density of $\mu \otimes \mathrm dV_2$. In general, let $u_{l,\varepsilon }=u_ l*\rho _\varepsilon $, which are smooth plurisubharmonic functions on $\Omega _{\varepsilon _0}$ for $\varepsilon <\varepsilon _0$, decreasing to $u_ l$ as $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$ (proposition 8.2.2 ). By theorem 9.2.5 , applied on $\Omega _{\varepsilon _0}\times \Delta $ to the functions $u_{l,\varepsilon }\circ p$, which decrease to $u_ l\circ p$, the left-hand sides for $u_{l,\varepsilon }$ converge weakly to the left-hand side for $u_ l$. By the same theorem on $\Omega _{\varepsilon _0}$, the measures $\mu _\varepsilon =\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,\varepsilon }\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{n,\varepsilon }$ converge weakly to $\mu $; hence $\mu _\varepsilon \otimes \mathrm dV_2\to \mu \otimes \mathrm dV_2$, because for a test function $\varphi $ on $\Omega _{\varepsilon _0}\times \Delta $ we have $\int \varphi \, \mathrm d(\mu _\varepsilon \otimes \mathrm dV_2)=\int \Phi \, \mathrm d\mu _\varepsilon $ with $\Phi (z)=\int _\Delta \varphi (z,w)\, \mathrm dV_2(w)$, a test function on $\Omega _{\varepsilon _0}$ (differentiate under the integral sign). Since $\varepsilon _0$ is arbitrary, the claim follows from the smooth case. Now apply the case already proved in dimension $n+1$, with $q=n\le (n+1)-1$, to the compact sets $\widetilde K=K\times \{ |w|\le 1/2\} $ and $\widetilde L=L\times \{ |w|\le 3/4\} $ in $\Omega \times \Delta $; note that $\widetilde K\subset \operatorname{Int}\widetilde L$. By the claim and Fubini's theorem, the left-hand side of the estimate for $V\circ p$ and the $u_ l\circ p$ is $\frac\pi 4\int _ K|V|\, \mathrm d\mu $, while $\| V\circ p\| _{L^1(\widetilde L)}=\frac{9\pi }{16}\| V\| _{L^1(L)}$ and $\| u_ l\circ p\| _{L^\infty (\widetilde L)}=\| u_ l\| _{L^\infty (L)}$. Hence the estimate holds in $\mathbb C^ n$ with the constant $\frac94C_{\widetilde K,\widetilde L,n}$, which depends only on $K$, $L$ and $n$. This proves the case $q=n$. $\square$

title: Monge ampere capacity
text: Definition 9.3.2 . Let $D\subset \mathbb {C}^ n$, $n\ge 1$, be a bounded open set. The Monge–Ampère capacity of a Borel set $E\subset D$ is \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)=\sup \left\{ \int _ E(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n: v\in \mathrm{PSH}(D),\  0\le v\le 1\right\} .  \] The functions $v$ in this supremum are called competitors for $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$. The outer capacity of an arbitrary set $A\subset D$ is \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(A)=\inf \{ \operatorname {Cap}_ D(G):A\subset G\subset D, \  G\text{ open}\} .  \]

title: Bt capacity basic
text: Proposition 9.3.3 . Let $D\subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a bounded open set. The set functions $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$ and $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D$ are increasing with respect to inclusion and countably subadditive. Moreover: $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(K)<\infty $ for every compact $K\subset D$, and $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)=\sup \{ \operatorname {Cap}_ D(K):K\subset E\text{ compact}\} $ for every Borel set $E\subset D$; if $E_ j\subset D$ are Borel sets increasing to $E$, then $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E_ j)\to \operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)$; there is a constant $C_ D$ such that $|E|\le C_ D\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)$ for every Borel set $E\subset D$, where $|E|$ is Lebesgue measure; if $B\Subset D$ is a ball and $K\subset B$ is compact, there is a constant $C$ such that, for every Borel set $E\subset K$, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)\le \operatorname {Cap}_ B(E) \le C\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E),  \] and the same inequalities hold for the outer capacities of arbitrary subsets of $K$; both capacities are invariant under biholomorphisms between bounded open sets: if $F\colon D\to D'$ is biholomorphic, then $\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}(F(E))=\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)$ for Borel sets $E\subset D$ and $\operatorname {Cap}^*_{D'}(F(A))=\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(A)$ for arbitrary sets $A\subset D$. Proof. For each competitor $v$, the measure $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n$ is increasing and countably subadditive on Borel sets: $\int _{\bigcup _ jE_ j}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\le \sum _ j\int _{E_ j}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\le \sum _ j\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E_ j)$. Taking the supremum over $v$ gives the same properties for $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$. Outer capacity is increasing by definition. For countable subadditivity, given sets $A_ j$ with $\sum _ j\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(A_ j)<\infty $ and $\varepsilon >0$, choose open sets $G_ j\supset A_ j$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_ j)<\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(A_ j)+\varepsilon 2^{-j}$; then $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(\bigcup _ jA_ j)\le \operatorname {Cap}_ D(\bigcup _ jG_ j)\le \sum _ j\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(A_ j)+\varepsilon $. Finiteness on a compact set $K$ follows from theorem 9.1.3 with $T=1$, applied to $K$ and a compact neighborhood $L$ of $K$ in $D$, since $\| v\| _{L^\infty (L)}\le 1$ for every competitor. Inner regularity of each Radon measure $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n$ (definition 1.1.1 ) gives $\int _ E(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n=\sup _ K\int _ K(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\le \sup _ K\operatorname {Cap}_ D(K)$ over compact $K\subset E$, and taking the supremum over $v$ gives (1). For (2), $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E_ j)\le \operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)$ by monotonicity, and for every competitor $v$ monotone convergence gives $\int _ E(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n=\lim _ j\int _{E_ j}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\le \lim _ j\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E_ j)$; taking the supremum over $v$ gives (2). For (3), choose $a\in D$ and $d>0$ with $D\subset B(a,d)$; the function $|z-a|^2/d^2$ is a competitor, and by ( 9.2 ) and proposition 9.1.2 (3) its Monge–Ampère measure is $n!\pi ^{-n}d^{-2n}\, \mathrm dV_{2n}$. Hence (3) holds with $C_ D=\pi ^ nd^{2n}/n!$. For (4), the first inequality holds because the restriction to $B$ of a competitor for $D$ is a competitor for $B$, with the same Monge–Ampère measure on $B$. For the second, write $B=B(a,r)$ and choose $\lambda >0$ such that $\rho =\lambda (|z-a|^2-r^2)<-1$ on a neighborhood of $K$. Given a competitor $v$ for $B$, let $w$ be the function equal to $\max \{ v-1,\rho \} $ on $B$ and to $\rho $ on $D\setminus B$. Since $v-1\le 0$ on $B$ and $\rho =0$ on $\partial B$, proposition 8.2.5 shows that $w$ is plurisubharmonic on $D$. It equals $v-1$ near $K$, satisfies $w\ge -1$ on $D$, and is bounded above by $\Lambda =\max \{ 0,\sup _ D\rho \} $, which does not depend on $v$. Thus $(w+1)/(\Lambda +1)$ is a competitor for $D$, and by locality its Monge–Ampère measure near $K$ is $(\Lambda +1)^{-n}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n$. This gives the second inequality with $C=(\Lambda +1)^ n$; the first inequality holds for all Borel subsets of $B$. For the outer capacities in (4), let $K'$ be a compact neighborhood of $K$ in $B$; the constant obtained for $K'$ also serves for $K$, and we use it. If $A\subset K$ and $G$ is an open subset of $D$ or of $B$ containing $A$, then $G\cap \operatorname{Int}K'$ is open in both $B$ and $D$, contains $A$, lies in $K'$, and has no larger capacity than $G$. Applying the inequalities to these sets and taking infima over $G$ gives them for the outer capacities of $A$. For (5), let $F\colon D\to D'$ be biholomorphic. By proposition 8.2.3 , applied to $F$ and to $F^{-1}$, the map $v\mapsto v\circ F$ is a bijection from the competitors for $D'$ onto the competitors for $D$, and by proposition 9.1.2 (5), $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v\circ F))^ n=F^*\bigl ((\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\bigr )$. We claim that for every positive Radon measure $\mu $ on $D'$, regarded as a current of bidegree $(n,n)$, the pullback $F^*\mu $ is the image of $\mu $ under $F^{-1}$, that is, $\int \psi \, \mathrm d(F^*\mu )=\int \psi \circ F^{-1}\, \mathrm d\mu $ for every test function $\psi $ on $D$. If $\mu =g\, \mathrm dV_{2n}$ with $g$ smooth, then $F^*\mu =(g\circ F)\, |\det F'|^2\, \mathrm dV_{2n}$, because $F^*(\mathrm dz_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm dz_ n)=\det F'\, \mathrm dz_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm dz_ n$ and similarly for the conjugate forms; since $|\det F'|^2$ is the Jacobian determinant of $F$ as a map of $\mathbb R^{2n}$, the change of variables formula gives the claim. Both sides of the claimed identity are weakly continuous in $\mu $ (proposition 7.5.2 ), and on relatively compact open subsets of $D'$ every $\mu $ is the weak limit of its smooth regularizations, so the claim holds in general. Consequently $(F^*\mu )(F^{-1}(E'))=\mu (E')$ for Borel sets $E'\subset D'$, since two Radon measures that agree on test functions agree on Borel sets (proposition 1.4.3 (4)). Applying this to $\mu =(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n$ and $E'=F(E)$ and taking the supremum over $v$ gives $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(E)=\operatorname {Cap}_{D'}(F(E))$. Since $F$ is a homeomorphism, it maps the open sets containing a set $A$ bijectively onto the open sets containing $F(A)$, so the outer capacities agree as well. $\square$

title: Bt poles zero capacity
text: Proposition 9.3.4 . Let $D\subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a bounded open set, let $K,L\subset D$ be compact sets with $K\subset \operatorname{Int}L$, and let $V\in \mathrm{PSH}(D)$. There is a constant $C_{K,L}$, depending only on $K$, $L$ and $n$, such that \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ V<-s\} ) \le \frac{C_{K,L}}{s}\| V\| _{L^1(L)},\qquad s>0.  \] Moreover, let $E\subset D$ be a set locally contained in pole sets of plurisubharmonic functions, that is, every point of $D$ has an open neighborhood $W\subset D$ and a plurisubharmonic function $V_ W$ on $W$ with $E\cap W\subset \{ V_ W=-\infty \} $. (Such sets are called pluripolar in chapter 10 .) Then $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(E\cap K)=0$ for every compact set $K\subset D$, and $E$ is contained in a Borel set which has measure zero for every measure $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ n$ with locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions $u_1,\ldots ,u_ n$ on $D$. Proof. Choose an open neighborhood $U$ of $K$ with compact closure in $\operatorname{Int}L$. For every competitor $v$, theorem 9.3.1 , applied to $\overline U\subset \operatorname{Int}L$ with $q=n$ and $u_1=\cdots =u_ n=v$, gives \[  \int _{U\cap \{ V<-s\} }(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\le s^{-1}\int _{\overline U}|V|\, (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n \le C s^{-1}\| V\| _{L^1(L)}.  \] Since $V$ is upper semicontinuous, $U\cap \{ V<-s\} $ is an open set containing $K\cap \{ V<-s\} $; taking the supremum over $v$ proves the estimate. Since $V$ is locally integrable (theorem 8.2.1 ), $\| V\| _{L^1(L)}<\infty $, and letting $s\to \infty $ gives $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(K\cap \{ V=-\infty \} )=0$. Now let $E$ be as in the statement. Let $x\in D$, let $W$ and $V_ W$ be as in the hypothesis, and choose $r>0$ with $\overline{B(x,3r)}\subset W$; put $B_ x=B(x,3r)$, $K_ x=\overline{B(x,r)}$ and $L_ x=\overline{B(x,2r)}$. Then $E\cap B_ x\subset \{ V_ W=-\infty \} $, and the restriction of $V_ W$ to $B_ x$ is plurisubharmonic. The estimate just proved, applied in $B_ x$ to this restriction and to $K_ x\subset \operatorname{Int}L_ x$, gives $\operatorname {Cap}^*_{B_ x}(E\cap K_ x)=0$; since every open set in $B_ x$ is open in $D$, the first inequality of proposition 9.3.3 (4) gives $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(E\cap K_ x)=0$. A compact set $K\subset D$ is covered by finitely many interiors $\operatorname{Int}K_ x$, and subadditivity gives $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(E\cap K)=0$. Finally, by theorem 9.3.1 , applied on $B_ x$ to $K_ x\subset \operatorname{Int}L_ x$ with $q=n$, the function $V_ W$ is integrable on $K_ x$ for every measure $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ n$ as in the statement, so the Borel set $K_ x\cap \{ V_ W=-\infty \} $ has measure zero for all these measures. Since $D$ has a countable basis, countably many sets $\operatorname{Int}K_ x$ cover $D$, and the union of the corresponding sets $K_ x\cap \{ V_ W=-\infty \} $ is a Borel set with the required property. $\square$

title: Błocki
text: Proposition 9.3.5 (Błocki) . Let $B$ be a ball, and let $u$ and $h$ be bounded plurisubharmonic functions on a neighborhood of $\overline B$ with $u\le h$ on $B$ and $u=h$ on a collar of $\partial B$. Let $v$ be a bounded plurisubharmonic function on a neighborhood of $\overline B$, and put $M=\sup _ Bv-\inf _ Bv$. Then \[  \int _ B(h-u)^{n+1}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n \le (n+1)!M^ n\int _ B(h-u)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ n.  \] Proof. First suppose that $u$, $h$ and $v$ are smooth; then $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u$, $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v$ are positive $(1,1)$-forms, by proposition 8.2.2 . Subtracting $\sup _ Bv$ from $v$, we may assume $-M\le v\le 0$ on $B$. Put $w=h-u\ge 0$; it vanishes on a collar of $\partial B$. Let $p\ge 2$, and let $R$ be a smooth closed strongly positive form of bidegree $(n-1,n-1)$; the exterior product of $R$ with a positive $(1,1)$-form is then a nonnegative multiple of the volume form, by proposition 7.2.1 , since positive $(1,1)$-forms are strongly positive. Since $\mathrm{d}w\wedge \mathrm{d}^{\mathrm c}w$ is a positive $(1,1)$-form by ( 9.7 ) and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h\wedge R\ge 0$, the chain rule $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w^ p)=pw^{p-1}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w+p(p-1)w^{p-2}\mathrm dw\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}w$ gives \[  \begin{aligned}  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w^ p)\wedge R& =\bigl (p w^{p-1}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}h-\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u) +p(p-1)w^{p-2}\mathrm{d}w\wedge \mathrm{d}^{\mathrm c}w\bigr )\wedge R\\ & \ge -pw^{p-1}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge R. \end{aligned}  \] Since $w^ p$ has compact support in $B$ and $R$ is closed, ( 9.1 ) gives $\int _ Bw^ p\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v\wedge R=(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(vR))(w^ p)=(vR)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w^ p))$. As $v\le 0$ and $-v\le M$, the preceding inequality therefore yields \[  \int _ Bw^ p\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v\wedge R =\int _ Bv\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w^ p)\wedge R \le pM\int _ Bw^{p-1}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u\wedge R.  \] For $k=1,\ldots ,n$, apply this with $p=n+2-k$ and $R=(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{n-k}\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^{k-1}$, a product of positive $(1,1)$-forms, hence strongly positive (proposition 7.2.1 ) and closed. This gives \[  \int _ Bw^{n+2-k}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{n+1-k}\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^{k-1}\le (n+2-k)M\int _ Bw^{n+1-k}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{n-k}\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ k,  \] and chaining these $n$ inequalities from $k=1$ to $k=n$ gives the asserted inequality, since $(n+1)n\cdots 2=(n+1)!$. In general, write $B=B(a,r)$ and let $V$ be a collar of $\partial B$ on which $u=h$. Since $\partial B$ is compact, there is $r''<r$ with $\{ z:r''\le |z-a|\le r\} \subset V$; choose $r'\in (r'',r)$ and put $B'=B(a,r')$. Then $h-u$ vanishes on $B\setminus \overline{B(a,r'')}$. Convolve $u$, $h$ and $v$ with the same radial kernel $\rho _\varepsilon $, with $\varepsilon <\min \{ (r'-r'')/2,r-r'\} $ so small that the regularizations are defined, smooth and plurisubharmonic on a neighborhood of $\overline{B'}$ (proposition 8.2.2 ). At points of $\overline{B'}$ they are averages over balls of radius $\varepsilon $ contained in $B$, where $u\le h$; hence $u_\varepsilon \le h_\varepsilon $ on $\overline{B'}$. Moreover $h_\varepsilon -u_\varepsilon $ vanishes on the collar $\{ z:r''+\varepsilon <|z-a|<r-\varepsilon \} $ of $\partial B'$ and outside $\overline{B(a,r''+\varepsilon )}$ in $B'$, hence outside the compact set $\overline{B(a,(r'+r'')/2)}\subset B'$. The values of $v_\varepsilon $ on $B'$ are averages of values of $v$ on $B$, so the oscillation of $v_\varepsilon $ on $B'$ is at most $M$. Apply the smooth case on $B'$ and let $\varepsilon =\varepsilon _ k\downarrow 0$. The weights $(h_\varepsilon -u_\varepsilon )^{n+1}$ and $h_\varepsilon -u_\varepsilon $ are polynomials in decreasing sequences of bounded plurisubharmonic functions, and they, as well as their limits $(h-u)^{n+1}$ and $h-u$, vanish in $B'$ outside the fixed compact set $\overline{B(a,(r'+r'')/2)}$. Testing against a function $\chi \in C^\infty _ c(B')$ equal to $1$ on this set, corollary 9.2.6 lets both sides pass to the limit. Since $h-u$ vanishes on $B\setminus B'$, the limiting inequality on $B'$ is the asserted inequality on $B$. $\square$

title: Blocki capacity bound
text: 9.20 \begin{equation} \label{eq:blocki-capacity-bound} \begin{aligned}  \operatorname {Cap}_ D\bigl (B\cap \{ h-u>\delta \} \bigr ) & \le \sup _ v\frac{1}{\delta ^{n+1}}\int _ B(h-u)^{n+1}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n\\ & \le \frac{(n+1)!}{\delta ^{n+1}}\int _ B(h-u)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ n, \end{aligned} \end{equation}

title: Quasi-continuity and convergence in capacity
text: 9.4 Quasi-continuity and convergence in capacity Throughout this section and the next, $D\subset \mathbb {C}^ n$, $n\ge 1$, is a bounded open set. By theorem 4.5.2 , locally integrable subharmonic functions are quasi-continuous in the sense of 1 : they are continuous outside open sets of arbitrarily small relative capacity. We now define quasi-continuity with respect to the Monge–Ampère capacity instead, which is the meaning of the term in the rest of the book, prove that plurisubharmonic functions are quasi-continuous in this sense, and then show that the products are continuous under convergence in capacity. Definition 9.4.1 . A Borel function $f\colon D\to [-\infty ,\infty ]$ is quasi-continuous (for $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$) if for every compact set $K\subset D$ and every $\varepsilon >0$ there is an open set $G\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $ such that the restriction of $f$ to $K\setminus G$ is continuous. Here $[-\infty ,\infty ]$ carries its order topology. The same definition applies to a function defined on an open subset $W\subset D$, with compact sets $K\subset W$ and still with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$. The sum $f_1+f_2$ and the difference $f_1-f_2$ of two real-valued quasi-continuous functions $f_1,f_2$ are quasi-continuous, and so is $\Phi \circ f_1$ for every continuous function $\Phi \colon \mathbb R\to \mathbb R$. Indeed, these functions are Borel. Given $K$ and $\varepsilon $, choose open sets $G_ i\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_ i)<\varepsilon /2$ such that $f_ i$ is continuous on $K\setminus G_ i$, $i=1,2$. Then $G=G_1\cup G_2$ satisfies $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $ by subadditivity (proposition 9.3.3 ), and $f_1+f_2$ and $f_1-f_2$ are continuous on $K\setminus G$, as sums and differences of continuous real functions there; similarly, $\Phi \circ f_1$ is continuous on $K\setminus G_1$. Theorem 9.4.2 . Let $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(D)$. For every $\varepsilon >0$ there is an open set $G\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $ which contains the pole set $\{ u=-\infty \} $ and such that the restriction of $u$ to $D\setminus G$ is finite and continuous. In particular $u$ is quasi-continuous. Proof. Step 1: locally bounded $u$. Let $u$ be locally bounded, $K\subset D$ compact and $\varepsilon >0$; we find an open set $G\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $ such that $u$ is continuous on $K\setminus G$. For each $x\in K$ choose $r_ x>0$ with $\overline{B(x,3r_ x)}\subset D$; finitely many balls $B(x_ i,r_{x_ i})$, $1\le i\le m$, cover $K$. Suppose that for each $i$ we find an open set $G_ i$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_ i)<\varepsilon /m$ such that $u$ is continuous on $\overline{B(x_ i,r_{x_ i})}\setminus G_ i$. Then $G=\bigcup _ iG_ i$ satisfies $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $, and $u$ is continuous on $K\setminus G$, because the finitely many sets $(K\setminus G)\cap \overline{B(x_ i,r_{x_ i})}$ are closed in $K\setminus G$ and cover it, and $u$ is continuous on each of them. We may therefore assume that $K=\overline{B'}$, where $B'=B(x,r)$, $B=B(x,2r)$ and $B_1=B(x,3r)$ satisfy $\overline{B_1}\subset D$. Subtracting a constant, we may assume that $-N\le u\le -1$ on $B_1$. Let $j>2/r$. Since $U=B(x,5r/2)$, a neighborhood of $\overline B$, lies at distance $r/2>1/j$ from $\mathbb C^ n\setminus B_1$, the regularization $u*\rho _{1/j}$ is smooth and plurisubharmonic on $U$ and takes values in $[-N,-1]$ there; moreover, $u*\rho _{1/j}$ decreases to $u$ as $j\to \infty $ (proposition 8.2.2 ). Put $\psi =|z-x|^2-4r^2$, choose $\delta >0$ with $\overline{B'}\subset \{ \psi <-\delta \} $, and let $g=\max \{ u,A\psi \} $ and $g_ j=\max \{ u*\rho _{1/j},A\psi \} $, with $A=N/\delta $, be the functions ( 9.8 ) on $U$. The $g_ j$ are continuous and plurisubharmonic on $U$ and decrease to $g$; moreover, $g=u$ on $\{ \psi <-\delta \} \supset \overline{B'}$, and $g_ j=g=A\psi $ on a collar of $\partial B$. For $\delta '>0$ put $G_{j,\delta '}=\{ z\in B:g_ j(z)-g(z)>\delta '\} $; it is open, because $g_ j$ is continuous and $g$ is upper semicontinuous. By ( 9.20 ), applied with $h=g_ j$, $u=g$ and $\delta '$ in place of $\delta $, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_{j,\delta '})\le \frac{(n+1)!}{\delta '^{n+1}}\int _ B(g_ j-g)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g)^ n.  \] The right-hand side tends to zero as $j\to \infty $ by dominated convergence: $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g)^ n$ has finite mass on $B$, since $g$ is bounded and plurisubharmonic near $\overline B$, and the functions $g_ j-g\ge 0$ are bounded on $B$ uniformly in $j$ and decrease to zero. Choose $j_1<j_2<\cdots $ such that $G_ l=G_{j_ l,2^{-l}}$ satisfies $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_ l)<\varepsilon 2^{-l}$, and let $G=\bigcup _ lG_ l$. Then $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $, and on $B\setminus G$ we have $0\le g_{j_ l}-g\le 2^{-l}$ for every $l$. Thus $g$ is a uniform limit of continuous functions on $B\setminus G$, hence continuous there; in particular $u=g$ is continuous on $\overline{B'}\setminus G$. Step 2: arbitrary $u$. Let $K\subset D$ be compact and $\varepsilon >0$. By proposition 9.3.4 , applied to $K$ and a compact neighborhood $L$ of $K$ in $D$, there is $s>0$ with $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(K\cap \{ u<-s\} )<\varepsilon /2$, and hence an open set $G_1\supset K\cap \{ u<-s\} $ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_1)<\varepsilon /2$. By Step 1, applied to the locally bounded plurisubharmonic function $\max \{ u,-s\} $, there is an open set $G_2$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_2)<\varepsilon /2$ such that $\max \{ u,-s\} $ is continuous on $K\setminus G_2$. On $K\setminus (G_1\cup G_2)$ we have $u\ge -s$, hence $u=\max \{ u,-s\} $. Thus $G=G_1\cup G_2$ contains $K\cap \{ u=-\infty \} $, $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $, and $u$ is finite and continuous on $K\setminus G$. Step 3: a single exceptional set. Choose compact sets $K_ l$ with $K_ l\subset \operatorname{Int}K_{l+1}$ and $\bigcup _ lK_ l=D$. By Step 2 there are open sets $G^{(l)}\supset K_ l\cap \{ u=-\infty \} $ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G^{(l)})<\varepsilon 2^{-l}$ such that $u$ is finite and continuous on $K_ l\setminus G^{(l)}$. Put $G=\bigcup _ lG^{(l)}$. Then $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $, and $G$ contains the pole set of $u$. Every $x\in D\setminus G$ lies in some $\operatorname{Int}K_ l$, and on the neighborhood $\operatorname{Int}K_ l\setminus G$ of $x$ in $D\setminus G$ the function $u$ is a restriction of the continuous function $u|_{K_ l\setminus G^{(l)}}$. Hence $u|_{D\setminus G}$ is finite and continuous. $\square$ In the proofs below we extend continuous functions from compact sets, using the following elementary case of Tietze's extension theorem. Lemma 9.4.3 . Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, let $F\subset X$ be compact, and let $f\colon F\to \mathbb R$ be continuous with $|f|\le a$. Then $f$ has a continuous extension $g\colon X\to \mathbb R$ with $|g|\le a$. Proof. If $F=\varnothing $ or $a=0$, take $g=0$. Otherwise, for $L>0$ put \[  f_ L(x)=\max \Bigl \{ -a,\min \bigl \{ a,\inf _{y\in F}(f(y)+L\, d(x,y))\bigr \} \Bigr \} ,\qquad x\in X.  \] The infimum is finite, since $f\ge -a$, and as an infimum of functions that are Lipschitz with constant $L$ it is Lipschitz with constant $L$; hence $f_ L$ is continuous and $|f_ L|\le a$. We claim that $f_ L\to f$ uniformly on $F$ as $L\to \infty $. Taking $y=x$ shows $f_ L\le f$ on $F$. Given $\eta >0$, uniform continuity of $f$ on the compact set $F$ gives $r>0$ with $|f(y)-f(x)|<\eta $ for $x,y\in F$ with $d(x,y)<r$. Let $Lr>2a$ and $x\in F$. Points $y\in F$ with $d(x,y)\ge r$ give $f(y)+L\, d(x,y)\ge -a+Lr>a\ge f(x)$, and the other points give $f(y)+L\, d(x,y)>f(x)-\eta $. Hence the infimum is at least $f(x)-\eta $, and so is $f_ L(x)$, because $a\ge f(x)>f(x)-\eta $ and $-a\le f(x)$. This proves the claim. Consequently there is a continuous $g_1$ on $X$ with $|g_1|\le a$ and $|f-g_1|\le a/2$ on $F$. Applying the same construction to $f-g_1$ on $F$, we find a continuous $g_2$ with $|g_2|\le a/2$ and $|f-g_1-g_2|\le a/4$ on $F$, and inductively continuous $g_ k$ with $|g_ k|\le 2^{1-k}a$ and $|f-g_1-\cdots -g_ k|\le 2^{-k}a$ on $F$. The series $\sum _ kg_ k$ converges uniformly on $X$; its sum is continuous and equals $f$ on $F$, and clamping it to $[-a,a]$, that is, replacing it by $\max \{ -a,\min \{ a,\sum _ kg_ k\} \} $, does not change its values on $F$. $\square$ Lemma 9.4.4 . Let $K,L\subset D$ be compact sets with $K\subset \operatorname{Int}L$, and let $f$ be a real Borel function which is defined and quasi-continuous on a neighborhood of $L$. Then, for every $\delta >0$, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ |f|>\delta \} ) \le \operatorname {Cap}_ D(L\cap \{ |f|>\delta /2\} ).  \] Proof. Let $\eta >0$. By quasi-continuity, applied to the compact set $L$, there is an open set $G\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\eta $ such that $f$ is continuous on $L\setminus G$; let $g$ be a continuous extension of $f|_{L\setminus G}$ to $\mathbb {C}^ n$ (lemma 9.4.3 ); here $f|_{L\setminus G}$ is bounded, being continuous on a compact set. The open set $G\cup (\operatorname{Int}L\cap \{ |g|>\delta /2\} )$ contains $K\cap \{ |f|>\delta \} $, since $K\subset \operatorname{Int}L$ and $g=f$ on $K\setminus G$. Its part outside $G$ is a Borel set contained in $L\cap \{ |f|>\delta /2\} $, because $g=f$ on $L\setminus G$. By monotonicity and subadditivity, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ |f|>\delta \} )\le \eta +\operatorname {Cap}_ D(L\cap \{ |f|>\delta /2\} ).  \] Let $\eta \downarrow 0$. $\square$ Definition 9.4.5 . A net $(f_ a)$ of Borel functions $f_ a\colon D\to [-\infty ,+\infty ]$ converges locally in capacity to a Borel function $f\colon D\to [-\infty ,+\infty ]$ if, for every compact set $K\subset D$ and every $\delta >0$, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ f_ a>f+\delta \} )\longrightarrow 0, \qquad \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ f_ a<f-\delta \} )\longrightarrow 0.  \] Here $\pm \infty +\delta =\pm \infty $ and $\pm \infty -\delta =\pm \infty $. For finite functions, $K\cap \{ |f_ a-f|>\delta \} $ is the union of the two sets in the definition, so by monotonicity and subadditivity of outer capacity the two conditions together are equivalent to $\operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ |f_ a-f|>\delta \} )\to 0$. Convergence locally in capacity is a local property: it holds on $D$ if and only if, for every ball $B\Subset D$, it holds on $B$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ B$ in place of $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$. Indeed, if it holds on $D$ and $K\subset B$ is compact, then proposition 9.3.3 (4) gives $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ B(A)\le C\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(A)$ for all $A\subset K$. Conversely, if it holds on every ball $B\Subset D$, cover a compact set $K\subset D$ by finitely many balls $B(x_ i,r_ i)$ with $\overline{B(x_ i,2r_ i)}\subset D$; for $A\subset K_ i=K\cap \overline{B(x_ i,r_ i)}$, proposition 9.3.3 (4) gives $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(A)\le \operatorname {Cap}^*_{B(x_ i,2r_ i)}(A)$, and subadditivity over $i$ gives the condition on $D$. In particular, for functions on an open set $W\subset D$, convergence locally in capacity with $\operatorname {Cap}_ W$ is equivalent to the same condition, for compact subsets of $W$, with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$, since both are equivalent to the condition on balls $B\Subset W$. Proposition 9.4.6 . Let $u_ j$ be locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions on $D$ decreasing to a locally bounded function $u$. Then $u_ j\to u$ locally in capacity. Moreover, a net of real Borel functions on $D$ which is uniformly bounded on each compact subset of $D$ and converges locally in capacity to a locally bounded real Borel function also converges in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$. Proof. Let $K\subset D$ be compact and $\delta >0$. Since $u_ j\ge u$, the sets $\{ u_ j<u-\delta \} $ are empty, and we must show that $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(K\cap \{ u_ j-u>\delta \} )\to 0$. By theorem 8.3.1 , $u$ is plurisubharmonic. Covering $K$ by finitely many balls $B(x,r)$ with $\overline{B(x,4r)}\subset D$ and using subadditivity of outer capacity, we may assume that $K\subset \overline{B(x,r)}$ for such a ball; put $L=\overline{B(x,3r/2)}$, $B=B(x,3r)$ and $B_1=B(x,4r)$. We first make the functions coincide near $\partial B$. Since $u\le u_ j\le u_1$, all these functions are bounded on $B_1$ uniformly in $j$, so there are constants $c$ and $N\ge 1$ with $-N\le u_ j-c,\, u-c\le -1$ on $B_1$. Put $\psi =|z-x|^2-9r^2$, choose $\delta _0>0$ with $L\subset \{ \psi <-\delta _0\} $, and let $\hat u_ j=\max \{ u_ j-c,A\psi \} $ and $\hat u=\max \{ u-c,A\psi \} $, with $A=N/\delta _0$, be the functions ( 9.8 ) on $B_1$, with $\delta _0$ in place of $\delta $. They are bounded and plurisubharmonic on $B_1$, $\hat u_ j\downarrow \hat u$, $\hat u_ j-\hat u=u_ j-u$ on $L$, and $\hat u_ j=\hat u$ on a collar of $\partial B$. By ( 9.20 ), applied with $u=\hat u$ and $h=\hat u_ j$, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D\bigl (B\cap \{ \hat u_ j-\hat u>\delta /2\} \bigr ) \le (n+1)!\, (2/\delta )^{n+1}\int _ B(\hat u_ j-\hat u)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\hat u)^ n,  \] and the right-hand side tends to zero by dominated convergence, since $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\hat u)^ n$ has finite mass on $B$ and $0\le \hat u_ j-\hat u\le \hat u_1-\hat u$ decreases to zero. The real function $w_ j=u_ j-u$ is quasi-continuous on $D$, as a difference of two real quasi-continuous functions (theorem 9.4.2 and the remark following definition 9.4.1 ), and $w_ j=\hat u_ j-\hat u$ on $L$. Hence lemma 9.4.4 gives \[  \operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(K\cap \{ w_ j>\delta \} )\le \operatorname {Cap}_ D(L\cap \{ w_ j>\delta /2\} )\le \operatorname {Cap}_ D\bigl (B\cap \{ \hat u_ j-\hat u>\delta /2\} \bigr )\longrightarrow 0.  \] For the second assertion, let $f_ a\to f$ be as in the statement, let $K\subset D$ be compact, and let $M$ bound $|f_ a|$ and $|f|$ on $K$. Splitting $K$ into the Borel set where $|f_ a-f|>\delta $ and its complement, and using proposition 9.3.3 (3) together with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D\le \operatorname {Cap}^*_ D$ on Borel sets, we get \[  \int _ K|f_ a-f|\, \mathrm{d}V_{2n} \le 2MC_ D\operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ |f_ a-f|>\delta \} ) +\delta |K|.  \] Taking the limit along the net and then letting $\delta \downarrow 0$ proves $L^1$ convergence on $K$. $\square$ Lemma 9.4.7 . Let $B\subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a ball, and let $\mathcal U$ be a family of plurisubharmonic functions on $B$ which is uniformly bounded on each compact subset of $B$. For every compact set $K\subset B$ there is a constant $C$ such that, for all integers $0\le q\le n$, all $u_1,\ldots ,u_ q\in \mathcal U$ and all Borel sets $E\subset K$, the trace measure $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \beta ^{n-q}$, and the total variation of every coefficient measure of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q$, give $E$ mass at most $C\operatorname {Cap}_ B(E)$. Let $S_ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{q,j}$ with $u_{l,j}\in \mathcal U$, and suppose that $S_ j\to S$ weakly. Let $f_ j$ be real Borel functions on $B$, uniformly bounded on each compact subset of $B$, which converge locally in capacity (for $\operatorname {Cap}_ B$) to a real Borel function $f$ that is locally bounded and quasi-continuous. Then $f_ jS_ j\to fS$ weakly, and the same holds for the trace measures of $S_ j$ and $S$. This applies in particular to a fixed weight $f_ j=f$. Proof. (1) Let $B=B(a,R)$, fix $K$, and choose $R'<R$ with $K\subset B'=B(a,R')$. Let $M\ge 1$ be a common bound for $|u|$ on $B'$, $u\in \mathcal U$. For $u_1,\ldots ,u_ q\in \mathcal U$ put $v_ l=(u_ l+M)/(2M)$ and $\phi =|z-a|^2/R'^2$; these functions take values in $[0,1]$ on $B'$, and so does \[  F=\frac1n\bigl (v_1+\cdots +v_ q+(n-q)\phi \bigr ),  \] which is therefore a competitor for $\operatorname {Cap}_{B'}$. Expand $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}F)^ n$ by additivity, positive homogeneity and symmetry (proposition 9.1.2 , theorem 9.2.5 ). All terms are positive measures, and those in which each $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ l$ occurs once and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\phi $ occurs $n-q$ times add up to $c_{n,q}\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ q\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\phi )^{n-q}$, where $c_{n,q}=n^{-n}\, n!\, (n-q)^{n-q}/(n-q)!>0$ (with $0^0=1$) is the corresponding multinomial coefficient. Hence $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ q\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\phi )^{n-q}\le c_{n,q}^{-1}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}F)^ n$. Since $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\phi =\beta /(\pi R'^2)$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ l=2M\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ l$, it follows that $\int _ E\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \beta ^{n-q}\le C\operatorname {Cap}_{B'}(E)$ for Borel $E\subset B'$. The bound for the coefficient measures follows from theorem 7.2.5 , and proposition 9.3.3 (4), applied to $B'\Subset B$ and $K$, replaces $\operatorname {Cap}_{B'}$ by $\operatorname {Cap}_ B$ on subsets of $K$. (2) The weak limit $S$ is a positive current (theorem 7.2.5 ). Let $\sigma _ j$ be either the trace measure or a coefficient measure of $S_ j$, and $\sigma $ the corresponding measure of $S$; then $\int \psi \, \mathrm d\sigma _ j\to \int \psi \, \mathrm d\sigma $ for every test function $\psi $, since this integral is the value of $S_ j$ on a test form. Fix a continuous function $\chi $ with compact support in $B$ and a compact set $K\subset B$ with $\operatorname{Supp}\chi \subset \operatorname{Int}K$, and let $C$ be the constant of (1) for $K$; in particular $|\sigma _ j|(K)\le C\operatorname {Cap}_ B(K)$, which is finite by proposition 9.3.3 (1). A similar bound holds for $\sigma $ on open subsets $U\subset \operatorname{Int}K$: for the trace measure, which is the vague limit of the trace measures of $S_ j$ (section 7.2 ), proposition 1.5.2 gives $\sigma (U)\le \varliminf _ j\sigma _ j(U)\le C\operatorname {Cap}_ B(U)$, and the total variations of the coefficient measures of the positive current $S$ are bounded by a constant multiple of its trace measure. Since the total variations $|\sigma _ j|(K)$ are bounded, the convergence $\int \psi \, \mathrm d\sigma _ j\to \int \psi \, \mathrm d\sigma $ extends to continuous functions $\psi $ with support in $\operatorname{Int}K$: approximating $\psi $ uniformly by test functions supported in a fixed compact subset of $\operatorname{Int}K$ (lemma 1.4.1 (5)) changes the integrals by at most $\sup |\psi -\psi _\varepsilon |$ times a bound for $|\sigma _ j|(K)$ and $|\sigma |(K)$. Consider first the fixed weight $f$, and let $\eta >0$. Since $f$ is quasi-continuous, there is an open set $G\subset B$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ B(G)<\eta $ such that $f$ is continuous on $K\setminus G$; let $g$ be a continuous extension of $f|_{K\setminus G}$ to $\mathbb C^ n$ with $\sup |g|\le \sup _ K|f|$ (lemma 9.4.3 ). Then \[  \Bigl |\int \chi f\, \mathrm{d}\sigma _ j-\int \chi g\, \mathrm{d}\sigma _ j\Bigr |\le 2\sup _ K|f|\sup |\chi |\, |\sigma _ j|(G\cap \operatorname{Supp}\chi )\le C'\eta ,  \] and similarly for $\sigma $, using the open set $G\cap \operatorname{Int}K$. Since $\chi g$ is continuous with support in $\operatorname{Int}K$, we have $\int \chi g\, \mathrm{d}\sigma _ j\to \int \chi g\, \mathrm{d}\sigma $. Hence $\varlimsup _ j|\int \chi f\, \mathrm{d}\sigma _ j-\int \chi f\, \mathrm{d}\sigma |\le 2C'\eta $ for every $\eta >0$, which proves $f\sigma _ j\to f\sigma $. For varying weights, let $M_ K$ bound $|f_ j|$ and $|f|$ on $K$, and let $\delta >0$. By (1), \[  \Bigl |\int \chi (f_ j-f)\, \mathrm{d}\sigma _ j\Bigr | \le \sup |\chi |\Bigl (\delta \, C\operatorname {Cap}_ B(K)+2M_ KC\operatorname {Cap}^*_ B\bigl (K\cap \{ |f_ j-f|>\delta \} \bigr )\Bigr ).  \] As $j\to \infty $, the second term tends to zero by convergence in capacity; then we let $\delta \downarrow 0$. Together with the fixed-weight case, this proves $f_ j\sigma _ j\to f\sigma $, and hence $f_ jS_ j\to fS$. $\square$ Theorem 9.4.8 . Let $0\le q\le n$ be an integer. For $1\le l\le q$, let $(u_{l,j})_{j\ge 1}$ be a sequence of plurisubharmonic functions on $D$, uniformly bounded on each compact subset of $D$, which converges locally in capacity to a locally bounded plurisubharmonic function $u_ l$. Then \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{q,j} \longrightarrow \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q  \] weakly. More generally, if $f_ j$ are real Borel functions on $D$, uniformly bounded on each compact subset of $D$, which converge locally in capacity to a locally bounded, quasi-continuous real Borel function $f$, then $f_ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{q,j}\to f\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q$ weakly. Proof. Weak convergence is local (lemma 9.2.4 ), so it suffices to prove the convergence on every ball $B\Subset D$. By the remark following definition 9.4.5 , the convergence in capacity holds with $\operatorname {Cap}_ B$ in place of $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$ on every ball $B\Subset D$. The limit $f$ is quasi-continuous for $\operatorname {Cap}_ B$ as well: if $K\subset B$ is compact, $K'$ is a compact neighborhood of $K$ in $B$, and $G\subset D$ is open with $f$ continuous on $K'\setminus G$, then $G\cap \operatorname{Int}K'$ is open in $B$, $f$ is continuous on $K\setminus (G\cap \operatorname{Int}K')=K\setminus G$, and $\operatorname {Cap}_ B(G\cap \operatorname{Int}K')\le C\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)$ by proposition 9.3.3 (4) applied to $K'$. Finally, the functions $u_{l,j}$ and $u_ l$, restricted to $B$, form a family which is uniformly bounded on compact subsets of $B$. We may therefore work on such a ball and use lemma 9.4.7 . We argue by induction on $q$. For $q=0$ the product is $1$, and the weighted assertion is the second part of the lemma with $S_ j=1$. Let $q\ge 1$, and assume that $S_ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{2,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{q,j}$ converges weakly to $S=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q$. The functions $u_{1,j}$ converge in capacity to $u_1$, which is quasi-continuous by theorem 9.4.2 ; hence the second part of the lemma gives $u_{1,j}S_ j\to u_1S$, and applying $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ proves the unweighted assertion for $q$ factors. The weighted assertion then follows from the second part of the lemma once more. $\square$ Unlike theorem 9.2.5 , theorem 9.4.8 concerns only products with the base current $T=1$.

title: Quasi continuity
text: Definition 9.4.1 . A Borel function $f\colon D\to [-\infty ,\infty ]$ is quasi-continuous (for $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$) if for every compact set $K\subset D$ and every $\varepsilon >0$ there is an open set $G\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $ such that the restriction of $f$ to $K\setminus G$ is continuous. Here $[-\infty ,\infty ]$ carries its order topology.

title: Psh capacity quasicontinuity
text: Theorem 9.4.2 . Let $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(D)$. For every $\varepsilon >0$ there is an open set $G\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $ which contains the pole set $\{ u=-\infty \} $ and such that the restriction of $u$ to $D\setminus G$ is finite and continuous. In particular $u$ is quasi-continuous. Proof. Step 1: locally bounded $u$. Let $u$ be locally bounded, $K\subset D$ compact and $\varepsilon >0$; we find an open set $G\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $ such that $u$ is continuous on $K\setminus G$. For each $x\in K$ choose $r_ x>0$ with $\overline{B(x,3r_ x)}\subset D$; finitely many balls $B(x_ i,r_{x_ i})$, $1\le i\le m$, cover $K$. Suppose that for each $i$ we find an open set $G_ i$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_ i)<\varepsilon /m$ such that $u$ is continuous on $\overline{B(x_ i,r_{x_ i})}\setminus G_ i$. Then $G=\bigcup _ iG_ i$ satisfies $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $, and $u$ is continuous on $K\setminus G$, because the finitely many sets $(K\setminus G)\cap \overline{B(x_ i,r_{x_ i})}$ are closed in $K\setminus G$ and cover it, and $u$ is continuous on each of them. We may therefore assume that $K=\overline{B'}$, where $B'=B(x,r)$, $B=B(x,2r)$ and $B_1=B(x,3r)$ satisfy $\overline{B_1}\subset D$. Subtracting a constant, we may assume that $-N\le u\le -1$ on $B_1$. Let $j>2/r$. Since $U=B(x,5r/2)$, a neighborhood of $\overline B$, lies at distance $r/2>1/j$ from $\mathbb C^ n\setminus B_1$, the regularization $u*\rho _{1/j}$ is smooth and plurisubharmonic on $U$ and takes values in $[-N,-1]$ there; moreover, $u*\rho _{1/j}$ decreases to $u$ as $j\to \infty $ (proposition 8.2.2 ). Put $\psi =|z-x|^2-4r^2$, choose $\delta >0$ with $\overline{B'}\subset \{ \psi <-\delta \} $, and let $g=\max \{ u,A\psi \} $ and $g_ j=\max \{ u*\rho _{1/j},A\psi \} $, with $A=N/\delta $, be the functions ( 9.8 ) on $U$. The $g_ j$ are continuous and plurisubharmonic on $U$ and decrease to $g$; moreover, $g=u$ on $\{ \psi <-\delta \} \supset \overline{B'}$, and $g_ j=g=A\psi $ on a collar of $\partial B$. For $\delta '>0$ put $G_{j,\delta '}=\{ z\in B:g_ j(z)-g(z)>\delta '\} $; it is open, because $g_ j$ is continuous and $g$ is upper semicontinuous. By ( 9.20 ), applied with $h=g_ j$, $u=g$ and $\delta '$ in place of $\delta $, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_{j,\delta '})\le \frac{(n+1)!}{\delta '^{n+1}}\int _ B(g_ j-g)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g)^ n.  \] The right-hand side tends to zero as $j\to \infty $ by dominated convergence: $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}g)^ n$ has finite mass on $B$, since $g$ is bounded and plurisubharmonic near $\overline B$, and the functions $g_ j-g\ge 0$ are bounded on $B$ uniformly in $j$ and decrease to zero. Choose $j_1<j_2<\cdots $ such that $G_ l=G_{j_ l,2^{-l}}$ satisfies $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_ l)<\varepsilon 2^{-l}$, and let $G=\bigcup _ lG_ l$. Then $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $, and on $B\setminus G$ we have $0\le g_{j_ l}-g\le 2^{-l}$ for every $l$. Thus $g$ is a uniform limit of continuous functions on $B\setminus G$, hence continuous there; in particular $u=g$ is continuous on $\overline{B'}\setminus G$. Step 2: arbitrary $u$. Let $K\subset D$ be compact and $\varepsilon >0$. By proposition 9.3.4 , applied to $K$ and a compact neighborhood $L$ of $K$ in $D$, there is $s>0$ with $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(K\cap \{ u<-s\} )<\varepsilon /2$, and hence an open set $G_1\supset K\cap \{ u<-s\} $ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_1)<\varepsilon /2$. By Step 1, applied to the locally bounded plurisubharmonic function $\max \{ u,-s\} $, there is an open set $G_2$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G_2)<\varepsilon /2$ such that $\max \{ u,-s\} $ is continuous on $K\setminus G_2$. On $K\setminus (G_1\cup G_2)$ we have $u\ge -s$, hence $u=\max \{ u,-s\} $. Thus $G=G_1\cup G_2$ contains $K\cap \{ u=-\infty \} $, $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $, and $u$ is finite and continuous on $K\setminus G$. Step 3: a single exceptional set. Choose compact sets $K_ l$ with $K_ l\subset \operatorname{Int}K_{l+1}$ and $\bigcup _ lK_ l=D$. By Step 2 there are open sets $G^{(l)}\supset K_ l\cap \{ u=-\infty \} $ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G^{(l)})<\varepsilon 2^{-l}$ such that $u$ is finite and continuous on $K_ l\setminus G^{(l)}$. Put $G=\bigcup _ lG^{(l)}$. Then $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\varepsilon $, and $G$ contains the pole set of $u$. Every $x\in D\setminus G$ lies in some $\operatorname{Int}K_ l$, and on the neighborhood $\operatorname{Int}K_ l\setminus G$ of $x$ in $D\setminus G$ the function $u$ is a restriction of the continuous function $u|_{K_ l\setminus G^{(l)}}$. Hence $u|_{D\setminus G}$ is finite and continuous. $\square$

title: Compact tietze extension
text: Lemma 9.4.3 . Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space, let $F\subset X$ be compact, and let $f\colon F\to \mathbb R$ be continuous with $|f|\le a$. Then $f$ has a continuous extension $g\colon X\to \mathbb R$ with $|g|\le a$. Proof. If $F=\varnothing $ or $a=0$, take $g=0$. Otherwise, for $L>0$ put \[  f_ L(x)=\max \Bigl \{ -a,\min \bigl \{ a,\inf _{y\in F}(f(y)+L\, d(x,y))\bigr \} \Bigr \} ,\qquad x\in X.  \] The infimum is finite, since $f\ge -a$, and as an infimum of functions that are Lipschitz with constant $L$ it is Lipschitz with constant $L$; hence $f_ L$ is continuous and $|f_ L|\le a$. We claim that $f_ L\to f$ uniformly on $F$ as $L\to \infty $. Taking $y=x$ shows $f_ L\le f$ on $F$. Given $\eta >0$, uniform continuity of $f$ on the compact set $F$ gives $r>0$ with $|f(y)-f(x)|<\eta $ for $x,y\in F$ with $d(x,y)<r$. Let $Lr>2a$ and $x\in F$. Points $y\in F$ with $d(x,y)\ge r$ give $f(y)+L\, d(x,y)\ge -a+Lr>a\ge f(x)$, and the other points give $f(y)+L\, d(x,y)>f(x)-\eta $. Hence the infimum is at least $f(x)-\eta $, and so is $f_ L(x)$, because $a\ge f(x)>f(x)-\eta $ and $-a\le f(x)$. This proves the claim. Consequently there is a continuous $g_1$ on $X$ with $|g_1|\le a$ and $|f-g_1|\le a/2$ on $F$. Applying the same construction to $f-g_1$ on $F$, we find a continuous $g_2$ with $|g_2|\le a/2$ and $|f-g_1-g_2|\le a/4$ on $F$, and inductively continuous $g_ k$ with $|g_ k|\le 2^{1-k}a$ and $|f-g_1-\cdots -g_ k|\le 2^{-k}a$ on $F$. The series $\sum _ kg_ k$ converges uniformly on $X$; its sum is continuous and equals $f$ on $F$, and clamping it to $[-a,a]$, that is, replacing it by $\max \{ -a,\min \{ a,\sum _ kg_ k\} \} $, does not change its values on $F$. $\square$

title: Quasi continuous level capacity
text: Lemma 9.4.4 . Let $K,L\subset D$ be compact sets with $K\subset \operatorname{Int}L$, and let $f$ be a real Borel function which is defined and quasi-continuous on a neighborhood of $L$. Then, for every $\delta >0$, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ |f|>\delta \} ) \le \operatorname {Cap}_ D(L\cap \{ |f|>\delta /2\} ).  \] Proof. Let $\eta >0$. By quasi-continuity, applied to the compact set $L$, there is an open set $G\subset D$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)<\eta $ such that $f$ is continuous on $L\setminus G$; let $g$ be a continuous extension of $f|_{L\setminus G}$ to $\mathbb {C}^ n$ (lemma 9.4.3 ); here $f|_{L\setminus G}$ is bounded, being continuous on a compact set. The open set $G\cup (\operatorname{Int}L\cap \{ |g|>\delta /2\} )$ contains $K\cap \{ |f|>\delta \} $, since $K\subset \operatorname{Int}L$ and $g=f$ on $K\setminus G$. Its part outside $G$ is a Borel set contained in $L\cap \{ |f|>\delta /2\} $, because $g=f$ on $L\setminus G$. By monotonicity and subadditivity, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ |f|>\delta \} )\le \eta +\operatorname {Cap}_ D(L\cap \{ |f|>\delta /2\} ).  \] Let $\eta \downarrow 0$. $\square$

title: Local capacity convergence
text: Definition 9.4.5 . A net $(f_ a)$ of Borel functions $f_ a\colon D\to [-\infty ,+\infty ]$ converges locally in capacity to a Borel function $f\colon D\to [-\infty ,+\infty ]$ if, for every compact set $K\subset D$ and every $\delta >0$, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ f_ a>f+\delta \} )\longrightarrow 0, \qquad \operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ f_ a<f-\delta \} )\longrightarrow 0.  \] Here $\pm \infty +\delta =\pm \infty $ and $\pm \infty -\delta =\pm \infty $.

title: Psh decreasing capacity
text: Proposition 9.4.6 . Let $u_ j$ be locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions on $D$ decreasing to a locally bounded function $u$. Then $u_ j\to u$ locally in capacity. Moreover, a net of real Borel functions on $D$ which is uniformly bounded on each compact subset of $D$ and converges locally in capacity to a locally bounded real Borel function also converges in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$. Proof. Let $K\subset D$ be compact and $\delta >0$. Since $u_ j\ge u$, the sets $\{ u_ j<u-\delta \} $ are empty, and we must show that $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(K\cap \{ u_ j-u>\delta \} )\to 0$. By theorem 8.3.1 , $u$ is plurisubharmonic. Covering $K$ by finitely many balls $B(x,r)$ with $\overline{B(x,4r)}\subset D$ and using subadditivity of outer capacity, we may assume that $K\subset \overline{B(x,r)}$ for such a ball; put $L=\overline{B(x,3r/2)}$, $B=B(x,3r)$ and $B_1=B(x,4r)$. We first make the functions coincide near $\partial B$. Since $u\le u_ j\le u_1$, all these functions are bounded on $B_1$ uniformly in $j$, so there are constants $c$ and $N\ge 1$ with $-N\le u_ j-c,\, u-c\le -1$ on $B_1$. Put $\psi =|z-x|^2-9r^2$, choose $\delta _0>0$ with $L\subset \{ \psi <-\delta _0\} $, and let $\hat u_ j=\max \{ u_ j-c,A\psi \} $ and $\hat u=\max \{ u-c,A\psi \} $, with $A=N/\delta _0$, be the functions ( 9.8 ) on $B_1$, with $\delta _0$ in place of $\delta $. They are bounded and plurisubharmonic on $B_1$, $\hat u_ j\downarrow \hat u$, $\hat u_ j-\hat u=u_ j-u$ on $L$, and $\hat u_ j=\hat u$ on a collar of $\partial B$. By ( 9.20 ), applied with $u=\hat u$ and $h=\hat u_ j$, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D\bigl (B\cap \{ \hat u_ j-\hat u>\delta /2\} \bigr ) \le (n+1)!\, (2/\delta )^{n+1}\int _ B(\hat u_ j-\hat u)(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\hat u)^ n,  \] and the right-hand side tends to zero by dominated convergence, since $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\hat u)^ n$ has finite mass on $B$ and $0\le \hat u_ j-\hat u\le \hat u_1-\hat u$ decreases to zero. The real function $w_ j=u_ j-u$ is quasi-continuous on $D$, as a difference of two real quasi-continuous functions (theorem 9.4.2 and the remark following definition 9.4.1 ), and $w_ j=\hat u_ j-\hat u$ on $L$. Hence lemma 9.4.4 gives \[  \operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(K\cap \{ w_ j>\delta \} )\le \operatorname {Cap}_ D(L\cap \{ w_ j>\delta /2\} )\le \operatorname {Cap}_ D\bigl (B\cap \{ \hat u_ j-\hat u>\delta /2\} \bigr )\longrightarrow 0.  \] For the second assertion, let $f_ a\to f$ be as in the statement, let $K\subset D$ be compact, and let $M$ bound $|f_ a|$ and $|f|$ on $K$. Splitting $K$ into the Borel set where $|f_ a-f|>\delta $ and its complement, and using proposition 9.3.3 (3) together with $\operatorname {Cap}_ D\le \operatorname {Cap}^*_ D$ on Borel sets, we get \[  \int _ K|f_ a-f|\, \mathrm{d}V_{2n} \le 2MC_ D\operatorname {Cap}_ D^*(K\cap \{ |f_ a-f|>\delta \} ) +\delta |K|.  \] Taking the limit along the net and then letting $\delta \downarrow 0$ proves $L^1$ convergence on $K$. $\square$

title: Bounded product capacity domination
text: Lemma 9.4.7 . Let $B\subset \mathbb C^ n$ be a ball, and let $\mathcal U$ be a family of plurisubharmonic functions on $B$ which is uniformly bounded on each compact subset of $B$. For every compact set $K\subset B$ there is a constant $C$ such that, for all integers $0\le q\le n$, all $u_1,\ldots ,u_ q\in \mathcal U$ and all Borel sets $E\subset K$, the trace measure $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \beta ^{n-q}$, and the total variation of every coefficient measure of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q$, give $E$ mass at most $C\operatorname {Cap}_ B(E)$. Let $S_ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{q,j}$ with $u_{l,j}\in \mathcal U$, and suppose that $S_ j\to S$ weakly. Let $f_ j$ be real Borel functions on $B$, uniformly bounded on each compact subset of $B$, which converge locally in capacity (for $\operatorname {Cap}_ B$) to a real Borel function $f$ that is locally bounded and quasi-continuous. Then $f_ jS_ j\to fS$ weakly, and the same holds for the trace measures of $S_ j$ and $S$. This applies in particular to a fixed weight $f_ j=f$. Proof. (1) Let $B=B(a,R)$, fix $K$, and choose $R'<R$ with $K\subset B'=B(a,R')$. Let $M\ge 1$ be a common bound for $|u|$ on $B'$, $u\in \mathcal U$. For $u_1,\ldots ,u_ q\in \mathcal U$ put $v_ l=(u_ l+M)/(2M)$ and $\phi =|z-a|^2/R'^2$; these functions take values in $[0,1]$ on $B'$, and so does \[  F=\frac1n\bigl (v_1+\cdots +v_ q+(n-q)\phi \bigr ),  \] which is therefore a competitor for $\operatorname {Cap}_{B'}$. Expand $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}F)^ n$ by additivity, positive homogeneity and symmetry (proposition 9.1.2 , theorem 9.2.5 ). All terms are positive measures, and those in which each $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ l$ occurs once and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\phi $ occurs $n-q$ times add up to $c_{n,q}\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ q\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\phi )^{n-q}$, where $c_{n,q}=n^{-n}\, n!\, (n-q)^{n-q}/(n-q)!>0$ (with $0^0=1$) is the corresponding multinomial coefficient. Hence $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ q\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\phi )^{n-q}\le c_{n,q}^{-1}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}F)^ n$. Since $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\phi =\beta /(\pi R'^2)$ and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ l=2M\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ l$, it follows that $\int _ E\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \beta ^{n-q}\le C\operatorname {Cap}_{B'}(E)$ for Borel $E\subset B'$. The bound for the coefficient measures follows from theorem 7.2.5 , and proposition 9.3.3 (4), applied to $B'\Subset B$ and $K$, replaces $\operatorname {Cap}_{B'}$ by $\operatorname {Cap}_ B$ on subsets of $K$. (2) The weak limit $S$ is a positive current (theorem 7.2.5 ). Let $\sigma _ j$ be either the trace measure or a coefficient measure of $S_ j$, and $\sigma $ the corresponding measure of $S$; then $\int \psi \, \mathrm d\sigma _ j\to \int \psi \, \mathrm d\sigma $ for every test function $\psi $, since this integral is the value of $S_ j$ on a test form. Fix a continuous function $\chi $ with compact support in $B$ and a compact set $K\subset B$ with $\operatorname{Supp}\chi \subset \operatorname{Int}K$, and let $C$ be the constant of (1) for $K$; in particular $|\sigma _ j|(K)\le C\operatorname {Cap}_ B(K)$, which is finite by proposition 9.3.3 (1). A similar bound holds for $\sigma $ on open subsets $U\subset \operatorname{Int}K$: for the trace measure, which is the vague limit of the trace measures of $S_ j$ (section 7.2 ), proposition 1.5.2 gives $\sigma (U)\le \varliminf _ j\sigma _ j(U)\le C\operatorname {Cap}_ B(U)$, and the total variations of the coefficient measures of the positive current $S$ are bounded by a constant multiple of its trace measure. Since the total variations $|\sigma _ j|(K)$ are bounded, the convergence $\int \psi \, \mathrm d\sigma _ j\to \int \psi \, \mathrm d\sigma $ extends to continuous functions $\psi $ with support in $\operatorname{Int}K$: approximating $\psi $ uniformly by test functions supported in a fixed compact subset of $\operatorname{Int}K$ (lemma 1.4.1 (5)) changes the integrals by at most $\sup |\psi -\psi _\varepsilon |$ times a bound for $|\sigma _ j|(K)$ and $|\sigma |(K)$. Consider first the fixed weight $f$, and let $\eta >0$. Since $f$ is quasi-continuous, there is an open set $G\subset B$ with $\operatorname {Cap}_ B(G)<\eta $ such that $f$ is continuous on $K\setminus G$; let $g$ be a continuous extension of $f|_{K\setminus G}$ to $\mathbb C^ n$ with $\sup |g|\le \sup _ K|f|$ (lemma 9.4.3 ). Then \[  \Bigl |\int \chi f\, \mathrm{d}\sigma _ j-\int \chi g\, \mathrm{d}\sigma _ j\Bigr |\le 2\sup _ K|f|\sup |\chi |\, |\sigma _ j|(G\cap \operatorname{Supp}\chi )\le C'\eta ,  \] and similarly for $\sigma $, using the open set $G\cap \operatorname{Int}K$. Since $\chi g$ is continuous with support in $\operatorname{Int}K$, we have $\int \chi g\, \mathrm{d}\sigma _ j\to \int \chi g\, \mathrm{d}\sigma $. Hence $\varlimsup _ j|\int \chi f\, \mathrm{d}\sigma _ j-\int \chi f\, \mathrm{d}\sigma |\le 2C'\eta $ for every $\eta >0$, which proves $f\sigma _ j\to f\sigma $. For varying weights, let $M_ K$ bound $|f_ j|$ and $|f|$ on $K$, and let $\delta >0$. By (1), \[  \Bigl |\int \chi (f_ j-f)\, \mathrm{d}\sigma _ j\Bigr | \le \sup |\chi |\Bigl (\delta \, C\operatorname {Cap}_ B(K)+2M_ KC\operatorname {Cap}^*_ B\bigl (K\cap \{ |f_ j-f|>\delta \} \bigr )\Bigr ).  \] As $j\to \infty $, the second term tends to zero by convergence in capacity; then we let $\delta \downarrow 0$. Together with the fixed-weight case, this proves $f_ j\sigma _ j\to f\sigma $, and hence $f_ jS_ j\to fS$. $\square$

title: Bt capacity continuity
text: Theorem 9.4.8 . Let $0\le q\le n$ be an integer. For $1\le l\le q$, let $(u_{l,j})_{j\ge 1}$ be a sequence of plurisubharmonic functions on $D$, uniformly bounded on each compact subset of $D$, which converges locally in capacity to a locally bounded plurisubharmonic function $u_ l$. Then \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{q,j} \longrightarrow \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q  \] weakly. More generally, if $f_ j$ are real Borel functions on $D$, uniformly bounded on each compact subset of $D$, which converge locally in capacity to a locally bounded, quasi-continuous real Borel function $f$, then $f_ j\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{q,j}\to f\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q$ weakly. Proof. Weak convergence is local (lemma 9.2.4 ), so it suffices to prove the convergence on every ball $B\Subset D$. By the remark following definition 9.4.5 , the convergence in capacity holds with $\operatorname {Cap}_ B$ in place of $\operatorname {Cap}_ D$ on every ball $B\Subset D$. The limit $f$ is quasi-continuous for $\operatorname {Cap}_ B$ as well: if $K\subset B$ is compact, $K'$ is a compact neighborhood of $K$ in $B$, and $G\subset D$ is open with $f$ continuous on $K'\setminus G$, then $G\cap \operatorname{Int}K'$ is open in $B$, $f$ is continuous on $K\setminus (G\cap \operatorname{Int}K')=K\setminus G$, and $\operatorname {Cap}_ B(G\cap \operatorname{Int}K')\le C\operatorname {Cap}_ D(G)$ by proposition 9.3.3 (4) applied to $K'$. Finally, the functions $u_{l,j}$ and $u_ l$, restricted to $B$, form a family which is uniformly bounded on compact subsets of $B$. We may therefore work on such a ball and use lemma 9.4.7 . We argue by induction on $q$. For $q=0$ the product is $1$, and the weighted assertion is the second part of the lemma with $S_ j=1$. Let $q\ge 1$, and assume that $S_ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{2,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{q,j}$ converges weakly to $S=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q$. The functions $u_{1,j}$ converge in capacity to $u_1$, which is quasi-continuous by theorem 9.4.2 ; hence the second part of the lemma gives $u_{1,j}S_ j\to u_1S$, and applying $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ proves the unweighted assertion for $q$ factors. The weighted assertion then follows from the second part of the lemma once more. $\square$

title: Increasing limits and exceptional envelopes
text:
9.5 Increasing limits and exceptional envelopes The supremum of an increasing sequence of plurisubharmonic functions need not be upper semicontinuous, and it may differ from its upper semicontinuous regularization on an exceptional set. For instance, on the unit ball of $\mathbb C^ n$ the functions $\max \{ j^{-1}\log |z_1|,-1\} $ are plurisubharmonic (proposition 8.3.3 , proposition 8.2.5 ) and increase with $j$, since $\log |z_1|<0$ there; their supremum equals $0$ where $z_1
e 0$ and $-1$ on the hyperplane $\{ z_1=0\} $, while its upper semicontinuous regularization is $0$. We show that the products are nevertheless continuous along increasing sequences. The proof follows the pattern of the decreasing case: the inequality $u_{0,j}\le u_0$ bounds weak limits from above, while the quasi-continuity of the fixed weights, through lemma 9.4.7 , supplies the lower bound for the masses. As a consequence, the exceptional set of an upper envelope has outer capacity zero. Theorem 9.5.1 . Let $0\le q\le n$ be an integer. For $0\le l\le q$, let $(u_{l,j})_{j\ge 1}$ be an increasing sequence of locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions on $D$ which converges almost everywhere to a locally bounded plurisubharmonic function $u_ l$. Then \[   egin{aligned}  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{q,j} & \longrightarrow \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q,\  u_{0,j}\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{q,j} & \longrightarrow u_0\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q \end{aligned}  \] weakly. Moreover $u_{l,j}	o u_ l$ locally in capacity for every $l$. Proof. We first note that $u_{l,j}\le u_ l$ everywhere. Indeed, $u_{l,j}\le u_ l$ almost everywhere, so the plurisubharmonic functions $\max \{ u_{l,j},u_ l\} $ and $u_ l$ agree almost everywhere, and hence everywhere, by the uniqueness of plurisubharmonic representatives in theorem 8.2.1 , applied on each connected component of $D$. Consequently $u_{l,1}\le u_{l,j}\le u_ l$, and the sequences are uniformly bounded on each compact subset of $D$. As in the proof of theorem 9.2.5 , we prove the weighted assertion by induction on $q$, for all bounded open sets $D$ and all sequences as in the statement; convergence in capacity is proved at the end. For $q=0$ it follows from dominated convergence with respect to Lebesgue measure. Let $q\ge 1$ and assume the weighted assertion for $q-1$ factors; applying $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$ to it, with the weight $u_{1,j}$, gives the unweighted assertion for $q$ factors. Put $S_ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{q,j}$ and $S=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q$, so that $S_ j	o S$ weakly. Weak convergence is a local property (lemma 9.2.4 ). Fix $x\in D$ and $r>0$ with $\overline{B(x,4r)}\subset D$, and put $B=B(x,3r)$ and $B_1=B(x,4r)$; we prove the convergence on $B(x,2r)$. Subtracting constants does not affect the assertions, since the unweighted assertion for $q$ factors is known, so we may assume that $-N\le u_{l,j},u_ l\le -1$ on $B_1$ for all $l$ and $j$, where $N\ge 1$. Put $\psi =|z-x|^2-9r^2$, choose $\delta _0>0$ such that $\overline{B(x,2r)}\subset \{ \psi <-\delta _0\} $, and replace each function $v$ among the $u_{l,j}$ and $u_ l$ by the function $\max \{ v,A\psi \} $ of ( 9.8 ), with $U=B_1$, $\delta _0$ in place of $\delta $ and $A=N/\delta _0$. The new functions are plurisubharmonic on $B_1$ and take values in $[-N,0)$ on $B$; the new sequences still increase, satisfy $u_{l,j}\le u_ l$ and converge almost everywhere. The functions do not change on $B(x,2r)$, and by locality neither do the products. On the collar $V=\{ z\in B_1:\psi (z)>-1/A\} $ of $\partial B$ the new functions coincide with $A\psi $. By locality, on $V$ all the currents considered below coincide with fixed currents, independent of $j$ and $k$. Hence, if $\chi \in C^\infty _ c(B)$ equals $1$ on $B\setminus V$, the integral over $B$ of each of these currents splits into its integral against $\chi $, to which weak convergence applies, and its integral against $(1-\chi )\mathbf1_ B$, which only involves values on $V$ and therefore does not change; we use this without further comment. The currents $-u_{0,j}S_ j$ are positive on $B$, and their masses on compact subsets of $B$ are bounded uniformly in $j$ by theorem 9.1.3 ; by the compactness part of theorem 7.2.5 , every subsequence of $(u_{0,j}S_ j)$ has a further subsequence converging weakly on $B$. Let $\Theta $ be the limit of such a subsequence. Since $u_{0,j}\le u_0$, the currents $(u_0-u_{0,j})S_ j$ are positive. Let $\varphi $ be a strongly positive test form on $B$ of complementary bidegree. The positive measures $-u_0S_ j\wedge \varphi $ have bounded masses on compact sets, so by theorem 1.5.5 a further subsequence of $u_0S_ j\wedge \varphi $ converges weakly to some $
u $, and lemma 9.2.2 , applied to the constant sequence $f_ j=u_0$ and the measures $S_ j\wedge \varphi 	o S\wedge \varphi $, gives $
u \le u_0S\wedge \varphi $. The measures $(u_0-u_{0,j})S_ j\wedge \varphi $ are positive and converge along this subsequence to $
u -\Theta \wedge \varphi $, which is therefore positive. Hence $\Theta \wedge \varphi \le u_0S\wedge \varphi $. Evaluating this inequality of measures on a nonnegative test function equal to $1$ on $\operatorname{Supp}\varphi $, we get $(u_0S-\Theta )(\varphi )\ge 0$. Thus $u_0S-\Theta $ is a positive current on $B$, and it vanishes on $V$, since all the currents $u_{0,j}S_ j$ and $u_0S$ coincide there with $A\psi (A\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\psi )^ q$. Write $\gamma = eta ^{n-q}$. For fixed $k$ and all $j\ge k$, positivity of $S_ j\wedge \gamma $ and $u_{0,j}\ge u_{0,k}$ give \[  \int _ Bu_{0,j}S_ j\wedge \gamma \ge \int _ Bu_{0,k}S_ j\wedge \gamma .  \] Let $j	o \infty $ along the subsequence defining $\Theta $. The left-hand side tends to $\int _ B\Theta \wedge \gamma $. The fixed weight $u_{0,k}$ is quasi-continuous for $\operatorname {Cap}_ B$ by theorem 9.4.2 , and the functions $u_{l,j}$, $u_ l$ form a family which is uniformly bounded on $B$; so by lemma 9.4.7 (2) the right-hand side tends to $\int _ Bu_{0,k}S\wedge \gamma $. By the second assertion of corollary 9.2.6 , applied with $a=u_{0,k}$, $b=u_1$ and $R=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \gamma $, and by symmetry, \[  \int _ Bu_{0,k}S\wedge \gamma =\int _ Bu_1\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{0,k}\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \gamma .  \] As $k	o \infty $, the unweighted assertion for $q$ factors, already established, gives $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{0,k}\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q	o \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_0\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q$ weakly, and lemma 9.4.7 , with the fixed quasi-continuous weight $u_1$, passes the integral to the limit. A second application of corollary 9.2.6 identifies the limit with $\int _ Bu_0\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \gamma =\int _ Bu_0S\wedge \gamma $. We have shown that $\int _ B\Theta \wedge \gamma \ge \int _ Bu_0S\wedge \gamma $. Since $u_0S-\Theta $ is positive with compact support in $B$, its trace measure has total mass $\int _ B(u_0S-\Theta )\wedge \gamma \le 0$ and therefore vanishes, and $\Theta =u_0S$ by theorem 7.2.5 . Thus every subsequence of $(u_{0,j}S_ j)$ has a further subsequence converging weakly to $u_0S$ on $B$. Hence the whole sequence converges to $u_0S$ on $B$: otherwise there would be a test form $\varphi $ on $B$ and a subsequence along which $|(u_{0,j}S_ j-u_0S)(\varphi )|$ stays bounded away from zero, and no further subsequence of it could converge to $u_0S$. Since the modifications change neither the functions nor the weighted products on $B(x,2r)$, the original weighted products converge on $B(x,2r)$; this completes the induction. Now that both assertions are known for every $q\le n$, we prove convergence in capacity. Fix $l$, a compact set $K\subset D$ and $\delta >0$. Since $u_{l,j}\le u_ l$, the sets $\{ u_{l,j}>u_ l+\delta \} $ are empty. Covering $K$ by finitely many balls and using subadditivity of outer capacity, we may assume that $K\subset \overline{B(x,r)}$ with $\overline{B(x,4r)}\subset D$; put $L=\overline{B(x,3r/2)}$. Let $\hat u_{l,j}$ and $\hat u_ l$ be the functions obtained by the modification above, on $B=B(x,3r)$; on $\{ \psi <-\delta _0\} \supset L$ we have $\hat u_ l-\hat u_{l,j}=u_ l-u_{l,j}$. These functions are bounded and plurisubharmonic on $B_1$, they satisfy $\hat u_{l,j}\le \hat u_ l$, and both coincide with $A\psi $ on the collar $V$ of $\partial B$. By ( 9.20 ), applied with $u=\hat u_{l,j}$ and $h=\hat u_ l$, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D igl (B\cap \{ \hat u_ l-\hat u_{l,j}>\delta /2\}  igr )\le  rac{(n+1)!\, 2^{n+1}}{\delta ^{n+1}}\int _ B(\hat u_ l-\hat u_{l,j})(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\hat u_{l,j})^ n.  \] The right-hand side tends to zero: $\int _ B\hat u_ l(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\hat u_{l,j})^ n	o \int _ B\hat u_ l(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\hat u_ l)^ n$ by the unweighted assertion and lemma 9.4.7 (2) with the fixed quasi-continuous weight $\hat u_ l$, and $\int _ B\hat u_{l,j}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\hat u_{l,j})^ n	o \int _ B\hat u_ l(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\hat u_ l)^ n$ by the weighted assertion with all factors and the weight equal to $\hat u_{l,j}$; as before, the integrals over $B$ are split by a cutoff. The real function $u_ l-u_{l,j}$ is quasi-continuous on $D$ (theorem 9.4.2 and the remark following definition 9.4.1 ), so lemma 9.4.4 gives \[   egin{aligned}  \operatorname {Cap}^*_ D igl (K\cap \{ u_ l-u_{l,j}>\delta \}  igr )& \le \operatorname {Cap}_ D igl (L\cap \{ u_ l-u_{l,j}>\delta /2\}  igr )\ & \le \operatorname {Cap}_ D igl (B\cap \{ \hat u_ l-\hat u_{l,j}>\delta /2\}  igr )\longrightarrow 0. \end{aligned}  \] $\square$ Corollary 9.5.2 . Let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty family of plurisubharmonic functions on $D$ which is locally uniformly bounded above, and let $F=\sup _{v\in \mathcal F}v$ be its pointwise supremum and $F^*$ its upper semicontinuous regularization. Then $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(K\cap \{ F<F^*\} )=0$ for every compact set $K\subset D$. Proof. By theorem 8.3.2 , $u=F^*$ is plurisubharmonic, and there is a countable subfamily $\{ w_1,w_2,\ldots \} \subset \mathcal F$ with $(\sup _ kw_ k)^*=u$. The functions $v_ j=\max \{ w_1,\ldots ,w_ j\} $ are plurisubharmonic (proposition 8.2.5 ) and increase to $G=\sup _ kw_ k$, and $G=G^*=u$ almost everywhere by theorem 8.3.2 , applied to the countable family. Fix an integer $m\ge 1$. The functions $\max \{ v_ j,-m\} $ are locally bounded and plurisubharmonic on $D$, and they increase almost everywhere to the locally bounded plurisubharmonic function $\max \{ u,-m\} $, so by theorem 9.5.1 they converge to it locally in capacity. For rational $\delta >0$, the set where $\sup _ j\max \{ v_ j,-m\} <\max \{ u,-m\} -\delta $ is contained in $\{ \max \{ v_ k,-m\} <\max \{ u,-m\} -\delta \} $ for every $k$, and the outer capacities of the intersections of the latter sets with a compact set tend to zero as $k	o \infty $. Taking the union over rational $\delta $, countable subadditivity shows that the set \[  E_ m=\Bigl \{ \sup _ j\max \{ v_ j,-m\} <\max \{ u,-m\} \Bigr \}   \] meets every compact set in a set of outer capacity zero. If $\sup _ jv_ j(x)<u(x)$, then $u(x)>-\infty $, so $u(x)>-m$ for some integer $m$, and then $x\in E_ m$. Hence $\{ \sup _ jv_ j<u\} \subset  igcup _ mE_ m$ also meets every compact set in a set of outer capacity zero. Finally, $\sup _ jv_ j\le F\le u$, so $\{ F<F^*\} \subset \{ \sup _ jv_ j<u\} $. (Since outer capacity is defined for all sets, we need not know whether $\{ F<F^*\} $ is Borel.) $\square$

text:

The left-hand side tends to $\int _ B\Theta \wedge \gamma $. The fixed weight $u_{0,k}$ is quasi-continuous for $\operatorname {Cap}_ B$ by theorem 9.4.2 , and the functions $u_{l,j}$, $u_ l$ form a family which is uniformly bounded on $B$; so by lemma 9.4.7 (2) the right-hand side tends to $\int _ Bu_{0,k}S\wedge \gamma $. By the second assertion of corollary 9.2.6 , applied with $a=u_{0,k}$, $b=u_1$ and $R=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \gamma $, and by symmetry, \[  \int _ Bu_{0,k}S\wedge \gamma =\int _ Bu_1\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{0,k}\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \gamma .  \] As $k	o \infty $, the unweighted assertion for $q$ factors, already established, gives $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{0,k}\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q	o \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_0\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_2\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q$ weakly, and lemma 9.4.7 , with the fixed quasi-continuous weight $u_1$, passes the integral to the limit. A second application of corollary 9.2.6 identifies the limit with $\int _ Bu_0\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ q\wedge \gamma =\int _ Bu_0S\wedge \gamma $. We have shown that $\int _ B\Theta \wedge \gamma \ge \int _ Bu_0S\wedge \gamma $. Since $u_0S-\Theta $ is positive with compact support in $B$, its trace measure has total mass $\int _ B(u_0S-\Theta )\wedge \gamma \le 0$ and therefore vanishes, and $\Theta =u_0S$ by theorem 7.2.5 . Thus every subsequence of $(u_{0,j}S_ j)$ has a further subsequence converging weakly to $u_0S$ on $B$. Hence the whole sequence converges to $u_0S$ on $B$: otherwise there would be a test form $\varphi $ on $B$ and a subsequence along which $|(u_{0,j}S_ j-u_0S)(\varphi )|$ stays bounded away from zero, and no further subsequence of it could converge to $u_0S$. Since the modifications change neither the functions nor the weighted products on $B(x,2r)$, the original weighted products converge on $B(x,2r)$; this completes the induction. Now that both assertions are known for every $q\le n$, we prove convergence in capacity. Fix $l$, a compact set $K\subset D$ and $\delta >0$. Since $u_{l,j}\le u_ l$, the sets $\{ u_{l,j}>u_ l+\delta \} $ are empty. Covering $K$ by finitely many balls and using subadditivity of outer capacity, we may assume that $K\subset \overline{B(x,r)}$ with $\overline{B(x,4r)}\subset D$; put $L=\overline{B(x,3r/2)}$. Let $\hat u_{l,j}$ and $\hat u_ l$ be the functions obtained by the modification above, on $B=B(x,3r)$; on $\{ \psi <-\delta _0\} \supset L$ we have $\hat u_ l-\hat u_{l,j}=u_ l-u_{l,j}$. These functions are bounded and plurisubharmonic on $B_1$, they satisfy $\hat u_{l,j}\le \hat u_ l$, and both coincide with $A\psi $ on the collar $V$ of $\partial B$. By ( 9.20 ), applied with $u=\hat u_{l,j}$ and $h=\hat u_ l$, \[  \operatorname {Cap}_ D igl (B\cap \{ \hat u_ l-\hat u_{l,j}>\delta /2\}  igr )\le  rac{(n+1)!\, 2^{n+1}}{\delta ^{n+1}}\int _ B(\hat u_ l-\hat u_{l,j})(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\hat u_{l,j})^ n.  \] The right-hand side tends to zero: $\int _ B\hat u_ l(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\hat u_{l,j})^ n	o \int _ B\hat u_ l(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\hat u_ l)^ n$ by the unweighted assertion and lemma 9.4.7 (2) with the fixed quasi-continuous weight $\hat u_ l$, and $\int _ B\hat u_{l,j}(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\hat u_{l,j})^ n	o \int _ B\hat u_ l(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\hat u_ l)^ n$ by the weighted assertion with all factors and the weight equal to $\hat u_{l,j}$; as before, the integrals over $B$ are split by a cutoff. The real function $u_ l-u_{l,j}$ is quasi-continuous on $D$ (theorem 9.4.2 and the remark following definition 9.4.1 ), so lemma 9.4.4 gives \[   egin{aligned}  \operatorname {Cap}^*_ D igl (K\cap \{ u_ l-u_{l,j}>\delta \}  igr )& \le \operatorname {Cap}_ D igl (L\cap \{ u_ l-u_{l,j}>\delta /2\}  igr )\ & \le \operatorname {Cap}_ D igl (B\cap \{ \hat u_ l-\hat u_{l,j}>\delta /2\}  igr )\longrightarrow 0. \end{aligned}  \] $\square$

title: Psh envelope zero capacity
text: Corollary 9.5.2 . Let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty family of plurisubharmonic functions on $D$ which is locally uniformly bounded above, and let $F=\sup _{v\in \mathcal F}v$ be its pointwise supremum and $F^*$ its upper semicontinuous regularization. Then $\operatorname {Cap}^*_ D(K\cap \{ F<F^*\} )=0$ for every compact set $K\subset D$. Proof. By theorem 8.3.2 , $u=F^*$ is plurisubharmonic, and there is a countable subfamily $\{ w_1,w_2,\ldots \} \subset \mathcal F$ with $(\sup _ kw_ k)^*=u$. The functions $v_ j=\max \{ w_1,\ldots ,w_ j\} $ are plurisubharmonic (proposition 8.2.5 ) and increase to $G=\sup _ kw_ k$, and $G=G^*=u$ almost everywhere by theorem 8.3.2 , applied to the countable family. Fix an integer $m\ge 1$. The functions $\max \{ v_ j,-m\} $ are locally bounded and plurisubharmonic on $D$, and they increase almost everywhere to the locally bounded plurisubharmonic function $\max \{ u,-m\} $, so by theorem 9.5.1 they converge to it locally in capacity. For rational $\delta >0$, the set where $\sup _ j\max \{ v_ j,-m\} <\max \{ u,-m\} -\delta $ is contained in $\{ \max \{ v_ k,-m\} <\max \{ u,-m\} -\delta \} $ for every $k$, and the outer capacities of the intersections of the latter sets with a compact set tend to zero as $k\to \infty $. Taking the union over rational $\delta $, countable subadditivity shows that the set \[  E_ m=\Bigl \{ \sup _ j\max \{ v_ j,-m\} <\max \{ u,-m\} \Bigr \}   \] meets every compact set in a set of outer capacity zero. If $\sup _ jv_ j(x)<u(x)$, then $u(x)>-\infty $, so $u(x)>-m$ for some integer $m$, and then $x\in E_ m$. Hence $\{ \sup _ jv_ j<u\} \subset \bigcup _ mE_ m$ also meets every compact set in a set of outer capacity zero. Finally, $\sup _ jv_ j\le F\le u$, so $\{ F<F^*\} \subset \{ \sup _ jv_ j<u\} $. (Since outer capacity is defined for all sets, we need not know whether $\{ F<F^*\} $ is Borel.) $\square$

title: The homogeneous Dirichlet problem and balayage
text:
9.6 The homogeneous Dirichlet problem and balayage A plurisubharmonic function is maximal if it cannot be increased on a compact set without losing plurisubharmonicity (definition 9.6.5 ). We show in theorem 9.6.6 that, for locally bounded functions, maximality is equivalent to $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ n=0$. The proof replaces $u$ on a ball by a solution $H$ of the homogeneous equation $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}H)^ n=0$ with the same boundary values (corollary 9.6.4 ); in chapter 10 the same replacement shows that relative extremal functions have vanishing Monge–Ampère measure away from the sets on which they are constrained. We construct $H$ as an upper envelope. To show that it solves the equation, we bound its second differences by composing with automorphisms of the ball (lemma 9.6.1 ), which makes it twice differentiable almost everywhere (lemma 9.6.2 ). Lemma 9.6.1 . Let $B\subset \mathbb C^ n$ be the unit ball. For $a\in B$ and $h\in \mathbb C^ n$ with $|h|$ small, depending on $a$, there are biholomorphic automorphisms $S_{a,h}$ of $B$ such that $S_{a,0}$ is the identity and $S_{a,h}(a)=a+h$. Each $S_{a,h}$ extends to a holomorphic map on a neighborhood of $\overline B$ which maps $\partial B$ onto $\partial B$. For every compact set $K\subset B$ there is $h_0>0$ such that the map $(a,h,z)\mapsto S_{a,h}(z)$ is defined and smooth on an open subset of $\mathbb C^ n	imes \mathbb C^ n	imes \mathbb C^ n$ containing $K	imes \overline{B(0,h_0)}	imes \overline B$, and holomorphic in $z$ there. In particular, there is a constant $C$ such that, for $a\in K$, $|h|\le h_0$ and $z\in \overline B$, the first and second derivatives of $S_{a,h}(z)$ with respect to the real variable $h\in \mathbb C^ n=\mathbb R^{2n}$ are bounded by $C$. Proof.
