title: Mixed products energy capacity continuity
text: Corollary 9.10.14 . Let $E\geq 0$, and for $1\leq l\leq n$ and $j\geq 1$ let $u_{l,j}\in \mathcal E_0(B)$ with $e_1(u_{l,j})\leq E$. Suppose that, for each $l$, $u_{l,j}\to u_ l$ locally in capacity as $j\to \infty $, where $u_ l$ is a locally bounded plurisubharmonic function on $B$. Then \[  \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{n,j} \longrightarrow \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ n  \] weakly on $B$. Proof. We compare the products with those of the truncations at a level $-T$: the latter converge by theorem 9.4.8 , and by theorem 9.10.13 the two differ by a term of order $1/T$. For $T>0$ put $a_{l,j}=\max \{ u_{l,j},-T\} $, and write \[  R_ j=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{n,j},\qquad R_{j,T}=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a_{1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a_{n,j}.  \] By lemma 9.10.7 , $a_{l,j}\in \mathcal E_0(B)$ and $e_1(a_{l,j})\leq E$. For each $l$, theorem 9.10.13 with $u_0=u_{l,j}$, respectively $u_0=a_{l,j}$, gives \[  \int _ B(-u_{l,j})\, R_ j\leq C_ nE,\qquad \int _ B(-a_{l,j})\, R_{j,T}\leq C_ nE.  \] Let $D_{j,T}=\bigcup _{l=1}^ n\{ u_{l,j}\leq -T\} $. On $\{ u_{l,j}\leq -T\} $ both $-u_{l,j}$ and $-a_{l,j}$ are at least $T$, so Chebyshev's inequality gives \[  R_ j(D_{j,T})\leq nC_ nE/T,\qquad R_{j,T}(D_{j,T})\leq nC_ nE/T.  \] On the complement of $D_{j,T}$, every $u_{l,j}$ is greater than $-T$. For $0\leq k\leq n$ put \[  P_ k=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a_{1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a_{k,j}\wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{k+1,j}\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{n,j},  \] so that $P_0=R_ j$ and $P_ n=R_{j,T}$. By the symmetry of the products, $P_ k=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}a_{k,j}\wedge \Theta _ k$ and $P_{k-1}=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{k,j}\wedge \Theta _ k$ with the same closed positive current $\Theta _ k$ formed by the other $n-1$ factors, and maximum locality (proposition 9.2.7 with $p=1$, $u=u_{k,j}$, $v=-T$ and base current $\Theta _ k$) gives $P_ k=P_{k-1}$ on $\{ u_{k,j}>-T\} $. Hence $R_ j=R_{j,T}$ on the complement of $D_{j,T}$, and for every $\chi \in C_ c(B)$, \[  \left|\int _ B\chi \, (R_ j-R_{j,T})\right| \leq 2nC_ nE\| \chi \| _\infty /T.  \] Now fix $\chi \in C_ c(B)$, choose an open set $B'\Subset B$ containing $\operatorname{Supp}\chi $, and let $T>\max _ l\sup _{B'}|u_ l|$. By ( 9.53 ), the uniformly bounded functions $a_{l,j}$ converge to the locally bounded plurisubharmonic function $\max \{ u_ l,-T\} $ locally in capacity, and theorem 9.4.8 shows that $R_{j,T}\to \bigwedge _ l\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\max \{ u_ l,-T\} $ weakly on $B$. On $B'$ we have $\max \{ u_ l,-T\} =u_ l$, so by locality (proposition 9.1.2 ) this limit equals $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ n$ there. Consequently \[  \varlimsup _{j\to \infty }\left|\int _ B\chi \, R_ j-\int _ B\chi \, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ n\right|\leq 2nC_ nE\| \chi \| _\infty /T  \] for all large $T$, and letting $T\to \infty $ completes the proof. $\square$

title: Mixed products for a common measure
text:
9.11 Mixed products for a common measure Corollary 9.7.6 bounds a mixed Monge–Ampère product from below when the pure Monge–Ampère measures of the factors have continuous lower densities with respect to Lebesgue measure. For non-pluripolar products in chapter 15 we need the same inequality relative to an arbitrary positive Radon measure $\mu $, which may be singular with respect to Lebesgue measure. Instead of regularizing the potentials by convolution, as in the proof of that corollary, we restrict each pure Monge–Ampère measure to a compact set and replace it by its cube averages, as in proposition 9.10.3 . The averaged measures have piecewise constant densities, so the case of Lebesgue measure applies on each cube, and Hölder's inequality compares the resulting bound with the cube averages of the expected lower bound. The convergence results of section 9.10 then allow us to pass to the limit. Theorem 9.11.1 . Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb C^ n$ be open, $n\geq 1$, and let $u_1,\ldots ,u_ n$ be locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions on $\Omega $. Let $\mu $ be a positive Radon measure on $\Omega $, and let $f_1,\ldots ,f_ n$ be nonnegative Borel functions on $\Omega $. If \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ i)^ n\geq f_ i\mu \qquad (1\leq i\leq n),  \] then 9.75  egin{equation} \label{eq:bounded-multifactor-common-measure} \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ n \geq \left(\prod _{i=1}^ nf_ i^{1/n}ight)\mu . \end{equation} For $n=1$ the assertion is the hypothesis. text: Corollary 9.11.3 . Under the hypotheses of corollary 9.11.2 , \[  (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u+v))^ n\geq (f^{1/n}+g^{1/n})^ n\mu .  \] Proof. By additivity and symmetry of the products, $(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(u+v))^ n=\sum _{k=0}^ n\binom nk(\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ k\wedge (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^{n-k}$. Bound the terms with $1\leq k\leq n-1$ by corollary 9.11.2 and the terms with $k=0,n$ by the hypotheses; the binomial formula then gives the assertion. The density on the right is locally $\mu $-integrable, since $f^{k/n}g^{(n-k)/n}\leq f+g$ by the weighted arithmetic–geometric mean inequality, and $f$ and $g$ are locally $\mu $-integrable because $f\mu \leq (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u)^ n$ and $g\mu \leq (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v)^ n$. $\square$

title: Bounded complex Hessians and contact sets
text:
9.12 Bounded complex Hessians and contact sets Monge–Ampère measures of envelopes are computed on contact sets: if a potential $u$ lies below an obstacle $f$ and $u=f$ on a set $E$, one expects the Monge–Ampère measure of $u$ on $E$ to be determined by the Hessian of $f$. Applied to the smooth function $\sum _ jt_ ju_ j$ with $t_1,\ldots ,t_ n\in \mathbb R$, it gives the identity \[  \Bigl (\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\sum _ jt_ ju_ j\Bigr )^ n=\frac{n!}{\pi ^ n}\det \Bigl (\sum _ jt_ jA_ j\Bigr )\, \mathrm dV_{2n}  \] between exterior powers of smooth forms, and both sides are polynomials in $t_1,\ldots ,t_ n$. We compare the coefficients of $t_1\cdots t_ n$. Since $2$-forms commute, on the left this coefficient is $n!$ times the exterior product $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_1\wedge \cdots \wedge \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_ n$, which is the Bedford–Taylor product by proposition 9.1.2 (1); on the right it is $(n!)^2\pi ^{-n}D(A_1,\dots ,A_ n)\, \mathrm dV_{2n}$, by the definition of the mixed discriminant. This proves the first formula for smooth $u_ j$. For continuous $u_ j$, let $u_{j,\varepsilon }=u_ j*\rho _\varepsilon $ be their radial mollifications, which are smooth and plurisubharmonic on $\Omega _\varepsilon $ (proposition 8.2.2 ). They converge to $u_ j$ uniformly on compact sets (lemma 1.4.1 ), so their products converge weakly by proposition 9.1.4 . By proposition 1.4.3 , the complex Hessian matrix of $u_{j,\varepsilon }$ is the mollification $A_{j,\varepsilon }$ of the matrix $A_ j$ of locally bounded functions. Let $K\subset \Omega $ be compact. For small $\varepsilon $, the entries of $A_{j,\varepsilon }$ are bounded on $K$ by the bounds of the entries of $A_ j$ on a fixed compact neighborhood of $K$, and by lemma 1.4.1 they converge to those of $A_ j$ in $L^1(K)$. Products of functions which are bounded on $K$ uniformly in $\varepsilon $ and converge in $L^1(K)$ converge in $L^1(K)$, because $|ab-a'b'|\leq |a||b-b'|+|b'||a-a'|$. Since $D$ is a polynomial in the matrix entries, it follows that $D(A_{1,\varepsilon },\dots ,A_{n,\varepsilon })\to D(A_1,\dots ,A_ n)$ in $L^1(K)$. By the first part, $(n!/\pi ^ n)D(A_{1,\varepsilon },\dots ,A_{n,\varepsilon })\, \mathrm dV_{2n}$ is the product of the $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}u_{j,\varepsilon }$, so the weak limit of these products is $(n!/\pi ^ n)D(A_1,\dots ,A_ n)\, \mathrm dV_{2n}$. This proves the first formula in general. By lemma 9.12.2 , each $u_ j$ belongs to $W^{2,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega )\subset W^{2,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega )$, so proposition 9.12.3 , applied to $u_ j$ and the chosen representative of $v_ j$, gives $A_ j=B_ j$ almost everywhere on $\{ u_ j=v_ j\} $, hence on $E$. Substituting into the first formula proves the second, and also shows that $\mathbf1_ ED(B_1,\dots ,B_ n)=\mathbf1_ ED(A_1,\dots ,A_ n)$ is locally bounded. $\square$

title: Gradients against positive currents
text:
9.13 Gradients against positive currents Several later arguments differentiate the product $v\Theta $ of a bounded plurisubharmonic function $v$ and a closed positive current $\Theta $; examples are the proof that non-pluripolar products are closed (theorem 15.2.1 ) and cutoff arguments on compact manifolds. For smooth $v$ the derivative is $\mathrm dv\wedge \Theta $, and its size is controlled by the gradient measure $\mathrm dv\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}v\wedge \Theta $, with $\mathrm d^{\mathrm c}$ as in ( 7.6 ). We extend both objects, together with the chain rule, to locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions by decreasing approximation. In this section $\eta $ denotes a real one-form, not the form $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}|z|^2$ of the preceding sections. Throughout, $U\subset \mathbb C^ n$ is open and $\Theta $ is a closed positive current of bidimension $(1,1)$ on $U$, with trace measure $\mu =\Theta \wedge  eta $. We first describe $\Theta $ by a matrix of densities with respect to $\mu $. For $1\leq j,k\leq n$ let $
u _{jk}$ be the complex Radon measure $ rac{\mathrm i}{2\pi }\, \mathrm dz_ k\wedge \mathrm d ar z_ j\wedge \Theta $. Up to a constant factor, $
u _{jk}$ is a coefficient measure of $\Theta $, so by theorem 7.2.5 there is a constant $C$, depending only on $n$, with $|
u _{jk}|\leq C\mu $. Hence $C\mu +\operatorname{Re}
u _{jk}$ and $C\mu +\operatorname{Im}
u _{jk}$ are positive measures bounded by $2C\mu $, and lemma 1.7.1 , applied to them, gives bounded Borel functions $h_{jk}$ with \[   rac{\mathrm i}{2\pi }\, \mathrm dz_ k\wedge \mathrm d ar z_ j\wedge \Theta =h_{jk}\, \mu \qquad (1\leq j,k\leq n).  \] Since $\Theta $ is real (theorem 7.2.5 ), the complex conjugate of $
u _{jk}$ is $ rac{-\mathrm i}{2\pi }\, \mathrm d ar z_ k\wedge \mathrm dz_ j\wedge \Theta =
u _{kj}$; by the uniqueness of densities in lemma 1.7.1 , $h_{kj}= ar h_{jk}$ $\mu $-almost everywhere, so the matrix $H=(h_{jk})$ is Hermitian $\mu $-almost everywhere. Since $\sum _ j rac{\mathrm i}{2\pi }\, \mathrm dz_ j\wedge \mathrm d ar z_ j= eta /\pi $, summing the identities with $j=k$ gives $\operatorname {tr}H=1/\pi $ $\mu $-almost everywhere. We identify a $(1,0)$-form $\xi =\sum _ k\xi _ k\, \mathrm dz_ k$ with its coefficient vector $(\xi _1,\ldots ,\xi _ n)\in \mathbb C^ n$, and write $\langle a,bangle =\sum _ ja_ j ar b_ j$ on $\mathbb C^ n$. For a constant $(1,0)$-form $\xi $, the measure $(\mathrm i/2\pi )\, \xi \wedge  ar\xi \wedge \Theta =\langle H\xi ,\xi angle \mu $ is positive, because $\mathrm i\xi \wedge  ar\xi $ is a strongly positive form and $\Theta $ is positive; so $\langle H\xi ,\xi angle \geq 0$ $\mu $-almost everywhere. Applying this to the countably many $\xi $ with rational real and imaginary parts, and using that $\xi \mapsto \langle H\xi ,\xi angle $ is continuous, we see that $H$ is positive semidefinite $\mu $-almost everywhere. Changing $H$ on a $\mu $-null set, we may assume that it is Hermitian and positive semidefinite with trace $1/\pi $ everywhere. Its eigenvalues then lie in $[0,1/\pi ]$, so that $\langle H\xi ,\xi angle \leq |\xi |^2/\pi $. Let $H^{1/2}$ be the positive semidefinite square root of $H$. It is a bounded Borel function on $U$. Indeed, by the Weierstrass approximation theorem there are real polynomials $p_ m$ with $p_ m(t)	o \sqrt t$ uniformly on $[0,1/\pi ]$. Diagonalizing $H(x)$ by a unitary matrix, we see that every entry of $p_ m(H(x))-H(x)^{1/2}$ is bounded by $\sup _{[0,1/\pi ]}|p_ m(t)-\sqrt t|$. The entries of $p_ m(H)$ are polynomials in the $h_{jk}$, hence Borel functions, and so are their pointwise limits, the entries of $H^{1/2}$. Moreover $|H^{1/2}\xi |^2=\langle H\xi ,\xi angle \leq |\xi |^2/\pi $. For a real $C^1$ function $w$, the coefficient vector of the form $\partial w$ is $(\partial w/\partial z_ k)_{k=1}^ n$, and we denote it also by $\partial w$. Since $\mathrm dw\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}w=(\mathrm i/2\pi )\, \partial w\wedge  ar\partial w$ by ( 9.7 ), it follows that 9.82  egin{equation} \label{eq:current-gradient-density} \mathrm dw\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}w\wedge \Theta = igl |H^{1/2}\partial w igr |^2\mu . \end{equation} Thus, for a compact set $K\subset U$, the square of the energy seminorm $\| H^{1/2}\partial w\| _{L^2(K,\mu )}$ is the mass that $\mathrm dw\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}w\wedge \Theta $ gives to $K$. Similarly, let $\eta $ be a real one-form with continuous coefficients and $(1,0)$-part $\sum _ ke_ k\, \mathrm dz_ k$, and put $e=(e_1,\ldots ,e_ n)$ and $w_ k=\partial w/\partial z_ k$. Only the $(1,1)$-part \[  \sum _{j,k}(e_ k ar w_ j- ar e_ jw_ k)\, \mathrm dz_ k\wedge \mathrm d ar z_ j  \] of $\eta \wedge \mathrm dw$ contributes to $\eta \wedge \mathrm dw\wedge \Theta $, so that $\eta \wedge \mathrm dw\wedge \Theta =-2\pi \mathrm i igl (\langle He,\partial wangle -\langle H\partial w,eangle  igr )\mu $. Since $H$ is Hermitian, the second inner product is the complex conjugate of the first, and therefore 9.83  egin{equation} \label{eq:current-gradient-pairing} \eta \wedge \mathrm dw\wedge \Theta =4\pi \operatorname{Im} igl \langle H^{1/2}e,H^{1/2}\partial w igr angle \, \mu . \end{equation} Lemma 9.13.1 . Let $\Theta $ be a closed positive current of bidimension $(1,1)$ on an open set $U\subset \mathbb C^ n$, and let $v$ be a locally bounded plurisubharmonic function on $U$. Then the current $\mathrm d(v\Theta )$ has measure coefficients; we denote it by $\mathrm dv\wedge \Theta $. The current 9.84  egin{equation} \label{eq:bounded-current-gradient-measure} E_\Theta (v)=\mathrm dv\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}v\wedge \Theta =	frac 12\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v^2\Theta )-v\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v\wedge \Theta \end{equation} is a positive measure, the gradient measure of $v$ with respect to $\Theta $. If smooth plurisubharmonic functions $v_ l$ decrease to $v$ on a neighborhood of a compact set $K\subset U$, then their gradients $\partial v_ l$ converge in the energy seminorm on $K$, that is, $H^{1/2}\partial v_ l$ converges in $L^2(K,\mu )$. For every $f\in C^1(\mathbb R)$, 9.85  egin{equation} \label{eq:bounded-current-chain-rule} \mathrm d(f(v)\Theta )=f'(v)\, \mathrm dv\wedge \Theta . \end{equation} Finally, let $\eta $ be a compactly supported smooth real one-form on $U$, and let $	au \in C_ c(U)$, $	au \geq 0$, be equal to one on $\operatorname{Supp}\eta $. There is a constant $C_\eta $, depending only on $\eta $, such that for every bounded Borel function $a$, 9.86  egin{equation} \label{eq:current-gradient-cauchy-schwarz} \left|\int a\eta \wedge \mathrm dv\wedge \Theta ight|^2 \leq C_\eta \left(\int 	au E_\Theta (v)ight) \left(\int _{\operatorname{Supp}\eta }|a|^2\,  \Theta \wedge  eta ight). \end{equation} Proof. We approximate $v$ by smooth plurisubharmonic functions $v_ l$ and pass to the limit, first in the gradients (Step 1) and then in each assertion of the lemma (Steps 2–5). All assertions are local, so we fix a compact set $K\subset U$ and an open neighborhood $W\subset U$ of $K$ on which smooth plurisubharmonic functions $v_ l$ decrease to $v$. For the convergence assertion, $W$ and the $v_ l$ are given. Otherwise we take for $W$ a relatively compact open neighborhood of $K$ in $U$ and for $v_ l$ the radial mollifications $v*ho _{\varepsilon _ l}$, where $\varepsilon _ l\downarrow 0$ and $\varepsilon _1$ is less than the distance from $\overline W$ to $\mathbb C^ n\setminus U$; they are smooth and plurisubharmonic on $W$ and decrease to $v$ (proposition 8.2.2 ). Choose a compact set $K_1\subset W$ with $K\subset \operatorname{Int}K_1$, and a function $\sigma \in C^\infty _ c(W)$ with $\sigma \geq 0$ which equals one on a neighborhood of $K_1$. Since $v\leq v_ l\leq v_1$, the $v_ l$ are uniformly bounded on $\operatorname{Supp}\sigma $. Step 1. Convergence of the gradients. For a smooth real function $w$, we have $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w^2)=2\, \mathrm dw\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}w+2w\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w$, and $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w^2\Theta )=\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w^2)\wedge \Theta $ because $\Theta $ is closed. Hence \[  \mathrm dw\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}w\wedge \Theta =	frac 12\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(w^2\Theta )-w\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}w\wedge \Theta .  \] Apply this identity to $w=v_ l-v_ m$ and integrate against $\sigma $: \[  \int \sigma \, \mathrm dw\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}w\wedge \Theta =	frac 12\int (v_ l-v_ m)^2\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\sigma \wedge \Theta -\int \sigma (v_ l-v_ m)\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ l-v_ m)\wedge \Theta .  \] Both terms on the right tend to zero as $l,m	o \infty $. For the first, $|v_ l-v_ m|\leq v_ N-v$ for $l,m\geq N$, and $v_ N-v	o 0$ pointwise and boundedly on $\operatorname{Supp}\sigma $; since $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\sigma \wedge \Theta $ is a signed measure with total variation bounded by a multiple of $\mu $ on $\operatorname{Supp}\sigma $, dominated convergence applies. For the second, expand it into the four integrals $\int \sigma v_ p\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ q\wedge \Theta $ with $p,q\in \{ l,m\} $, taken with the signs $+,-,-,+$. Given indices $l_ k,m_ k	o \infty $, pass to a subsequence along which both are strictly increasing; then $v_{l_ k}$ and $v_{m_ k}$ decrease to $v$, and the weighted form of theorem 9.2.5 on $W$, with the base current $\Theta $, shows that each of the four integrals tends to $\int \sigma v\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v\wedge \Theta $. Their signed sum therefore tends to zero, and since this holds for a subsequence of every such pair of index sequences, the second term tends to zero as $l,m	o \infty $. Since $\sigma \geq 0$, $\sigma =1$ on $K_1$ and $\mathrm dw\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}w\wedge \Theta $ is the positive measure $|H^{1/2}\partial w|^2\mu $, by ( 9.82 ), the left side bounds $\| H^{1/2}\partial v_ l-H^{1/2}\partial v_ m\| _{L^2(K_1,\mu )}^2$. Consequently $H^{1/2}\partial v_ l$ is a Cauchy sequence in $L^2(K_1,\mu )$; let $\Gamma \in L^2(K_1,\mu )$ be its limit. In particular, $H^{1/2}\partial v_ l$ converges in $L^2(K,\mu )$, which is the convergence assertion. Step 2. The first derivative. Let $\eta $ be a smooth real one-form with compact support in $\operatorname{Int}K_1$, with $(1,0)$-part $\sum _ ke_ k\, \mathrm dz_ k$. By ( 9.83 ), \[  \int \eta \wedge \mathrm dv_ l\wedge \Theta =4\pi \int \operatorname{Im} igl \langle H^{1/2}e,H^{1/2}\partial v_ l igr angle \, \mathrm d\mu \longrightarrow 4\pi \int \operatorname{Im} igl \langle H^{1/2}e,\Gamma  igr angle \, \mathrm d\mu ,  \] since $H^{1/2}e$ is bounded and vanishes outside $K_1$, and $\mu (K_1)<\infty $. On the other hand, $\mathrm dv_ l\wedge \Theta =\mathrm d(v_ l\Theta )$ since $\Theta $ is closed, and $v_ l\Theta 	o v\Theta $ weakly on $W$ by dominated convergence on the coefficient measures; hence $\mathrm d(v_ l\Theta )	o \mathrm d(v\Theta )$ weakly. Therefore the pairing of $\mathrm d(v\Theta )$ with $\eta $, written $\int \eta \wedge \mathrm d(v\Theta )$, equals the last integral. Write $\langle H^{1/2}e,\Gamma angle =\sum _ ke_ kG_ k$, where $G_ k=\sum _ j(H^{1/2})_{jk} ar\Gamma _ j$ belongs to $L^2(K_1,\mu )\subset L^1(K_1,\mu )$, so that \[  4\pi \operatorname{Im} igl \langle H^{1/2}e,\Gamma  igr angle =\sum _ k igl (-2\pi \mathrm i\, G_ k\, e_ k+2\pi \mathrm i\,  ar G_ k\,  ar e_ k igr ).  \] Thus, on real test one-forms $\eta $ supported in $\operatorname{Int}K_1$, the current $\mathrm d(v\Theta )$ acts by integrating against $\mu $ the coefficients $e_ k$ and $ ar e_ k$ of $\eta $, multiplied by the functions $-2\pi \mathrm i\, G_ k$ and $2\pi \mathrm i\,  ar G_ k$, which are integrable on $K_1$. Every test one-form is a complex linear combination of two real ones, so on $\operatorname{Int}K_1$ the current $\mathrm d(v\Theta )$ has measure coefficients, which are absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu $ and finite on $K_1$. In particular, for a bounded Borel function $a$, \[  \int a\eta \wedge \mathrm dv\wedge \Theta =4\pi \int a\operatorname{Im} igl \langle H^{1/2}e,\Gamma  igr angle \, \mathrm d\mu .  \] Step 3. The gradient measure. Since $H^{1/2}\partial v_ l	o \Gamma $ in $L^2(K_1,\mu )$, the densities $|H^{1/2}\partial v_ l|^2$ converge to $|\Gamma |^2$ in $L^1(K_1,\mu )$, so the measures $\mathrm dv_ l\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}v_ l\wedge \Theta =|H^{1/2}\partial v_ l|^2\mu $ converge weakly on $\operatorname{Int}K_1$ to the positive measure $|\Gamma |^2\mu $. On the other hand, by the identity of Step 1, \[  \mathrm dv_ l\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}v_ l\wedge \Theta =	frac 12\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v_ l^2\Theta )-v_ l\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v_ l\wedge \Theta \longrightarrow 	frac 12\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}(v^2\Theta )-v\, \mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}v\wedge \Theta  \] weakly on $W$: the first term converges by dominated convergence on the coefficient measures of $v_ l^2\Theta $ and the weak continuity of $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}$, and the second by theorem 9.2.5 . Hence the right side of ( 9.84 ) is the positive measure $|\Gamma |^2\mu $ on $\operatorname{Int}K_1$. Since $K$ was arbitrary and $K\subset \operatorname{Int}K_1$, the current $E_\Theta (v)$, which does not involve the approximations, is a positive measure on $U$. Step 4. The Cauchy–Schwarz inequality. Let $\eta $, $	au $ and $a$ be as in the statement, and apply Steps 1–3 with $K=\operatorname{Supp}	au $; then $\operatorname{Supp}\eta \subset K\subset \operatorname{Int}K_1$. For a smooth real function $w$ on $W$, ( 9.83 ) and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality give \[  \left|\int a\eta \wedge \mathrm dw\wedge \Theta ight|^2 \leq 16\pi ^2\int _{\operatorname{Supp}\eta }|a|^2 igl |H^{1/2}e igr |^2\, \mathrm d\mu \int _{\operatorname{Supp}\eta } igl |H^{1/2}\partial w igr |^2\, \mathrm d\mu .  \] Since $|H^{1/2}e|^2\leq |e|^2/\pi $, we have $16\pi ^2|H^{1/2}e|^2\leq C_\eta $ with $C_\eta =16\pi \sup |e|^2$, which depends only on $\eta $. The second integral is at most $\int 	au \, \mathrm dw\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}w\wedge \Theta $, because $	au \geq 0$ and $	au =1$ on $\operatorname{Supp}\eta $. Apply this to $w=v_ l$ and let $l	o \infty $. The left side converges to $|\int a\eta \wedge \mathrm dv\wedge \Theta |^2$ by Step 2, since $a\, \operatorname{Im}\langle H^{1/2}e,H^{1/2}\partial v_ langle 	o a\, \operatorname{Im}\langle H^{1/2}e,\Gamma angle $ in $L^1(K_1,\mu )$, and $\int 	au \, \mathrm dv_ l\wedge \mathrm d^{\mathrm c}v_ l\wedge \Theta 	o \int 	au E_\Theta (v)$ by Step 3, since $	au $ is continuous with compact support in $\operatorname{Int}K_1$. This proves ( 9.86 ). Step 5. The chain rule. Both sides of ( 9.85 ) are complex-linear in $f$, so we may assume that $f$ is real. Let first $f$ be smooth. The functions $v_ l$ and $v$ take values in a compact interval $J$ on $\operatorname{Supp}\sigma $. Since $f(v_ l)	o f(v)$ boundedly, $f(v_ l)\Theta 	o f(v)\Theta $ weakly on $W$ by dominated convergence, and hence $\mathrm d(f(v_ l)\Theta )	o \mathrm d(f(v)\Theta )$. By the chain rule for smooth functions and the closedness of $\Theta $, $\mathrm d(f(v_ l)\Theta )=f'(v_ l)\, \mathrm dv_ l\wedge \Theta $. Moreover $f'(v_ l)H^{1/2}\partial v_ l	o f'(v)\Gamma $ in $L^2(K_1,\mu )$: the difference is \[  f'(v_ l) igl (H^{1/2}\partial v_ l-\Gamma  igr )+ igl (f'(v_ l)-f'(v) igr )\Gamma ,  \] where the first term tends to zero because $f'$ is bounded on $J$, and the second by dominated convergence. Now let $\eta $ be as in Step 2. Identity ( 9.83 ), multiplied by the continuous function $f'(v_ l)$, and Step 2 with $a=f'(v)$ give \[  \int \eta \wedge f'(v_ l)\, \mathrm dv_ l\wedge \Theta =4\pi \int \operatorname{Im} igl \langle H^{1/2}e,f'(v_ l)H^{1/2}\partial v_ l igr angle \, \mathrm d\mu \longrightarrow \int \eta \wedge f'(v)\, \mathrm dv\wedge \Theta .  \] Since the left side also tends to $\int \eta \wedge \mathrm d(f(v)\Theta )$, the currents $\mathrm d(f(v)\Theta )$ and $f'(v)\, \mathrm dv\wedge \Theta $ agree on $\operatorname{Int}K_1$. As $K$ was arbitrary, this proves ( 9.85 ) for smooth $f$. Now let $f\in C^1(\mathbb R)$, and let $f_ m=f*ho _{1/m}$ be its mollifications on $\mathbb R$. By proposition 1.4.3 and lemma 1.4.1 , $f_ m	o f$ and $f_ m'=f'*ho _{1/m}	o f'$ uniformly on compact subsets of $\mathbb R$. Since $v$ is locally bounded, $f_ m(v)	o f(v)$ and $f_ m'(v)	o f'(v)$ uniformly on compact subsets of $U$. As $\Theta $ and $\mathrm dv\wedge \Theta $ are currents of order zero, it follows that $f_ m(v)\Theta 	o f(v)\Theta $ and $f_ m'(v)\, \mathrm dv\wedge \Theta 	o f'(v)\, \mathrm dv\wedge \Theta $ weakly. Since $\mathrm d$ is weakly continuous, the identity $\mathrm d(f_ m(v)\Theta )=f_ m'(v)\, \mathrm dv\wedge \Theta $ passes to the limit. $\square$
